notes: If a skp file is loaded via the command line or double-clicking on a skp in explorer (which is also is the command line) then this observer will not be called. The Ruby interpreter in SketchUp is ...

methods.name: onQuit
methods.summary: The #onQuit method is called when SketchUp closes. This is useful if you need to clean up anything or store your application state upon close.

methods.name: onUnloadExtension
methods.summary: The #onUnloadExtension method is called when the user turns off a Ruby extension. This is useful for detecting if the user is deactivating some critical set of observers, for example, so you can warn them or cache your extension state.

params.name: extension_name
params.desc: The name of the extension just unloaded.

Sketchup::ArcCurve.summary: An ArcCurve is a Curve that makes up part of a circle. This is the underlying class for circles as well. You can think of ArcCurves as entities that were created with SketchUp's Arc or Circle drawing tools and Curves as entities that were created with the Freehand drawing tool.

methods.name: center
methods.summary: Instance Methods The center method is used to retrieve the Point3d that is at the center of the circular arc.

returns.desc: point - a Point3d at the center of the arc if successful

methods.example:
centerpoint = Geom::Point3d.new
# Create a circle perpendicular to the normal or Z axis
vector = Geom::Vector3d.new 0,0,1
vector2 = vector.normalize!
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.entities
edgearray = entities.add_circle centerpoint, vector2, 10
edge = edgearray[0]
arccurve = edge.curve
point = arccurve.center

methods.name: circular?
methods.summary: Checks if the ArcCurve is a circle.
methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
center_point = Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
normal_vector = Geom::Vector3d.new(0, 0, 1)
radius = 10
edges = entities.add_circle(center_point, normal_vector, radius)
curve = edges[0].curve
is_circular = curve.circular?

methods.name: end_angle
methods.summary: The #end_angle method is used to retrieve the angle of the end of the arc measured from the X axis in radians.
methods.example:
# Create a 1/2 circle, normal to the Z axis
start_a = 0.0
end_a = 180.degrees
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.entities
edges = entities.add_arc(ORIGIN, X_AXIS, Z_AXIS, 5, start_a, end_a)
arc_curve = edges.first.curve
end_angle = arc_curve.end_angle
notes: A bug in SketchUp 2017 and older will report the end-angle for some circles as more than 360 degrees. In such case, subtract 2 * PI from the end angle value.

methods.name: normal
methods.summary: The normal method retrieves a Vector3d that is perpendicular to the plane of the arc.

returns.desc: vector - a Vector3d object if successful

methods.example:
centerpoint = Geom::Point3d.new
# Create a circle perpendicular to the normal or Z axis
vector = Geom::Vector3d.new 0,0,1
vector2 = vector.normalize!
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.entities
edgearray = entities.add_circle centerpoint, vector2, 10
edge = edgearray[0]
arccurve = edge.curve
v = arccurve.normal

methods.name: plane
methods.summary: The plane method is used to retrieve the plane of the arc. Refer to the Geom module for instructions to create a plane.

returns.desc: plane - the plane of the arc if successful

methods.example:
centerpoint = Geom::Point3d.new
# Create a circle perpendicular to the normal or Z axis
vector = Geom::Vector3d.new 0,0,1
vector2 = vector.normalize!
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.entities
edgearray = entities.add_circle centerpoint, vector2, 10
edge = edgearray[0]
arccurve = edge.curve
plane = arccurve.plane

methods.name: radius
methods.summary: The radius method is used to retrieve the radius of the arc.

returns.desc: radius - the radius of the arc if successful

methods.example:
centerpoint = Geom::Point3d.new
# Create a circle perpendicular to the normal or Z axis
vector = Geom::Vector3d.new 0,0,1
vector2 = vector.normalize!
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.entities
edgearray = entities.add_circle centerpoint, vector2, 10
edge = edgearray[0]
arccurve = edge.curve
radius = arccurve.radius

methods.name: start_angle
methods.summary: The start_angle method is used to retrieve the angle of the start of the arc, measured from the X axis in radians.

returns.desc: angle - the angle of the start of the arc if successful

methods.example:
# Create a 1/4 circle, radius of 5, normal to the Z axis
center = Geom::Point3d.new 0, 0, -1
normal = Geom::Vector3d.new 0,0,1
xaxis = Geom::Vector3d.new 1,0,0
start_a = Math::PI/2
end_a = Math::PI
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.entities
edgearray = entities.add_arc center, xaxis, normal, 5, start_a, end_a
edge = edgearray[0]
arccurve = edge.curve
start_angle = arccurve.start_angle

methods.name: xaxis
methods.summary: The xaxis method is used to retrieve the X axis of the coordinate system for the curve. Note that the length of the returned vector is equal to the radius of the underlying curve.

returns.desc: vector - a Vector3d object if successful

methods.example:
centerpoint = Geom::Point3d.new
# Create a circle perpendicular to the normal or Z axis
vector = Geom::Vector3d.new 0,0,1
vector2 = vector.normalize!
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.entities
edgearray = entities.add_circle centerpoint, vector2, 10
edge = edgearray[0]
arccurve = edge.curve
v = arccurve.xaxis

methods.name: yaxis
methods.summary: The yaxis method is used to retrieve the Y axis of the coordinate system for the curve. Note that the length of the returned vector is equal to the radius of the underlying curve.

returns.desc: vector - a Vector3d object if successful

methods.example:
centerpoint = Geom::Point3d.new
# Create a circle perpendicular to the normal or Z axis
vector = Geom::Vector3d.new 0,0,1
vector2 = vector.normalize!
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.entities
edgearray = entities.add_circle centerpoint, vector2, 10
edge = edgearray[0]
arccurve = edge.curve
v = arccurve.yaxis

Sketchup::AttributeDictionaries.summary: The AttributeDictionaries class is a collection of all of the AttributeDictionary objects that are attached to a given Entity object. The Entity class is a popular parent class in SketchUp, meaning you can attach AttributeDictionaries to almost anything, from geometric items like edges and faces and components to more conceptual things like pages or materials.

methods.summary: Instance Methods Get an AttributeDictionary by name. Returns nil if there is none with the given name.

params.name: key
params.desc: The name of the attribute dictionary.

returns.desc: the dictionary

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
value = model.set_attribute("my_dictionary", "test", 110)
attrdicts = model.attribute_dictionaries
dict = attrdicts['my_dictionary']

methods.name: count
methods.summary: The count method is inherited from the Enumerable mix-in module.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.set_attribute('Example', 'Hello', 'World')
dictionaries = model.attribute_dictionaries
number = dictionaries.count

methods.name: delete
methods.summary: The delete method destroys a given AttributeDictionary. This AttributeDictionary can be passed directly or identified by its string name.

params.name: key_or_dict
params.desc: The name of the attribute dictionary to delete, or the dictionary object itself.

returns.desc: the modified AttributeDictionaries

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
attrdicts = model.attribute_dictionaries
# Deletes a dictionary called 'my_dictionary'
attrdicts.delete 'my_dictionary'
raises: ArgumentError if an advanced attribute dictionary is being deleted.

methods.name: each
methods.summary: The #each method is used to iterate through all of the attributes dictionaries.

returns.desc: nil

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
dictionaries = model.attribute_dictionaries
# Iterates through all dictionaries and prints to screen.
dictionaries.each { |dictionary| puts dictionary.name }

methods.name: length
methods.summary: The #length method returns the number of attribute dictionary objects in the collection.

returns.desc: the number of attribute dictionary objects in the collection.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.set_attribute('Example', 'Hello', 'World')
dictionaries = model.attribute_dictionaries
number = dictionaries.length

methods.name: size
methods.summary: The #size method is an alias of #length.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.set_attribute('Example', 'Hello', 'World')
dictionaries = model.attribute_dictionaries
number = dictionaries.size

Sketchup::AttributeDictionary.summary: The AttributeDictionary class allows you to attach arbitrary collections of attributes to a SketchUp entity. The attributes are defined by key/value pairs where the keys are strings. An Entity or Model object can have any number of AttributeDictionary objects (see the AttributeDictionaries class).

methods.summary: Instance Methods The [] method is used to retrieve the attribute with a given key.

params.name: key
params.desc: The name of the attribute.

returns.desc: the attribute stored under your key, or nil if not found

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
value = model.set_attribute "testdictionary", "test", 115
attrdicts = model.attribute_dictionaries
attrdict = attrdicts["testdictionary"]

# value will contain 115
value = attrdict["test"]

methods.summary: The set value ([]=) method is used to set the value of an attribute with a given key. Creates a new attribute for the given key if needed.

params.name: key
params.desc: The valid key.

params.name: value
params.types: Boolean, Integer, Float, Length, nil, String, Time, Array, Geom::Point3d, Geom::Vector3d
params.desc: The value to be set.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
value = model.set_attribute("testdictionary", "test", 110)
attrdicts = model.attribute_dictionaries
attrdict = attrdicts["testdictionary"]
value = attrdict["test2"] = 120
p value

methods.name: count
methods.summary: The count method is inherited from the Enumerable mix-in module.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.set_attribute('Example', 'Hello', 'World')
dictionary = model.attribute_dictionary('Example')
number = dictionary.count

methods.name: delete_key
methods.summary: The delete_key method is used to delete an attribute with a given key.

params.name: key
params.desc: The key to be deleted.

returns.desc: the value of the key

methods.example:
create_if_nil = true
model = Sketchup.active_model
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionary("test_dict", create_if_nil)
attrdict["attr_one"] = "one"
attrdict["attr_two"] = "two"

# Delete a key/value pair and get the deleted value.
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionaries['test_dict']
value = attrdict.delete_key("attr_one")

methods.name: each
methods.summary: The #each method iterate through all of the attributes.
methods.example:
create_if_nil = true
model = Sketchup.active_model
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionary("test_dict", create_if_nil)
attrdict["attr_one"] = "one"
attrdict["attr_two"] = "two"

# Iterates through all attributes and prints the key to the screen.
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionaries['test_dict']
attrdict.each { | key, value |
  puts "#{key} = #{value}"
}
notes: Don't remove content from this collection while iterating over it with #each. This would change the size of the collection and cause elements to be skipped as the indices change. Instead copy the ...

methods.name: each_key
methods.summary: The #each_key method is used to iterate through all of the attribute keys.
methods.example:
create_if_nil = true
model = Sketchup.active_model
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionary("test_dict", create_if_nil)
attrdict["attr_one"] = "one"
attrdict["attr_two"] = "two"

# iterates through all attributes and prints the key to the screen
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionaries['test_dict']
attrdict.each_key { |key| puts key }

methods.name: each_pair
methods.summary: The #each_pair method is an alias for #each.
methods.example:
create_if_nil = true
model = Sketchup.active_model
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionary("test_dict", create_if_nil)
attrdict["attr_one"] = "one"
attrdict["attr_two"] = "two"

# iterates through all attributes and prints the key to the screen
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionaries['test_dict']
attrdict.each_pair { | key, value |
  puts "#{key} = #{value}"
}

methods.name: empty?
methods.summary: The #empty? method is used to check if the attribute dictionary is empty.

returns.desc: true if the attribute dictionary is empty, false otherwise

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
attribute_dictionary = model.attribute_dictionary("example", true)
attribute_dictionary["attribute_one"] = "1"
attribute_dictionary.empty? # Returns false

methods.name: keys
methods.summary: The keys method is used to retrieve an array with all of the attribute keys.

returns.desc: an array of keys within the attribute dictionary if successful

methods.example:
create_if_nil = true
model = Sketchup.active_model
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionary "test_dict", create_if_nil
attrdict["attr_one"] = "one"
attrdict["attr_two"] = "two"

# Gets an array of keys
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionaries['test_dict']
keys = attrdict.keys

methods.name: length
methods.summary: The #length method is used to retrieve the size (number of elements) of an attribute dictionary.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.set_attribute('Example', 'Hello', 'World')
dictionary = model.attribute_dictionary('Example')
number = dictionary.length

methods.name: name
methods.summary: The name method is used to retrieve the name of an attribute dictionary.

returns.desc: the name of the attribute dictionary if successful

methods.example:
create_if_nil = true
model = Sketchup.active_model
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionary "test_dict", create_if_nil
attrdict["attr_one"] = "one"
attrdict["attr_two"] = "two"

puts attrdict.name

methods.name: size
methods.summary: The #size method is an alias of #length.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.set_attribute('Example', 'Hello', 'World')
dictionary = model.attribute_dictionary('Example')
number = dictionary.size

methods.name: values
methods.summary: The values method is used to retrieve an array with all of the attribute values.

returns.desc: an array of values within the attribute dictionary if successful

methods.example:
create_if_nil = true
model = Sketchup.active_model
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionary "test_dict", create_if_nil
attrdict["attr_one"] = "one"
attrdict["attr_two"] = "two"

# Gets an array of values
attrdict = model.attribute_dictionaries['test_dict']
values = attrdict.values

Sketchup::Axes.summary: SketchUp's drawing axes consist of three colored lines (red, green, blue), usually perpendicular to each other, displayed in the drawing area. The exception is when the user open an instance with a non-orthogonal transformation. The root model transformation is always orthogonal. The drawing axes are used by drawing tools to align the geometry it creates as well as affecting the inference engine.

methods.name: axes
methods.summary: Instance Methods The axes method returns the vectors representing the directions of the axes.

returns.desc: Array - an array of three vectors.

methods.example: xaxis, yaxis, zaxis = Sketchup.active_model.axes.axes

methods.name: origin
methods.summary: The #origin method returns the origin of the axes.
methods.example: point = Sketchup.active_model.axes.origin

methods.name: set
methods.summary: The #set method allows the axes to be manipulated. The axes must always be orthogonal, otherwise an error is thrown.

params.name: origin
params.desc: Point3d - The origin to set.

params.name: xaxis
params.desc: Vector3d - The x axis to set.

params.name: yaxis
params.desc: Vector3d - The y axis to set.

params.name: zaxis
params.desc: Vector3d - The z axis to set.

returns.desc: - the axes object being set.

methods.example:
xaxis = Geom::Vector3d.new(3, 5, 0)
yaxis = xaxis * Z_AXIS
Sketchup.active_model.axes.set([10,0,0], xaxis, yaxis, Z_AXIS)

methods.name: sketch_plane
methods.summary: The sketch_plane method returns a plane representing the ground plane of the axes.

returns.desc: Array - of 4 numbers that give the coefficients of a plane equation.

methods.example: plane = Sketchup.active_model.axes.sketch_plane

methods.name: to_a
methods.summary: The axes method returns the origin and vectors representing the axes.

returns.desc: Array - an array of a point and three vectors.

methods.example: point, xaxis, yaxis, zaxis = Sketchup.active_model.axes.to_a

methods.name: transformation
methods.summary: The #transformation method returns the transformation of the axes. This is useful when creating tools that respect the model's drawing axes.

returns.desc: - the transformation for the axes.

methods.example:
# Point for a rectangle.
points = [
  Geom::Point3d.new( 0,  0, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(10,  0, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(10, 20, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new( 0, 20, 0)
]
# Transform the points so they are local to the model axes. Otherwise
# they would be local to the model origin.
tr = Sketchup.active_model.axes.transformation
points.each { |point| point.transform!(tr) }
Sketchup.active_model.active_entities.add_face(points)

methods.name: xaxis
methods.summary: The #xaxis method returns the x axis of the axes.

returns.desc: - the x axis for the axes.

methods.example: vector = Sketchup.active_model.axes.xaxis

methods.name: yaxis
methods.summary: The #yaxis method returns the y axis of the axes.

returns.desc: - the y axis for the axes.

methods.example: vector = Sketchup.active_model.axes.yaxis

methods.name: zaxis
methods.summary: The #zaxis method returns the z axis of the axes.

returns.desc: - the z axis for the axes.

methods.example: vector = Sketchup.active_model.axes.zaxis

Sketchup::Behavior.summary: The Behavior class is used to control the "behavior" of components, which roughly correlates to the series of options that you see in the Components dialog under the "edit" tab, such as whether it casts shadows, glues to walls, etc. A Behavior object is accessed from a ComponentDefinition object, not created with a Behavior.new call.

methods.name: always_face_camera=
methods.summary: Instance Methods The always_face_camera= method is used to set the always_face_camera behavior for a component. If the always_face_camera behavior is true, a component will always try to orient itself so that the Y axis of the component is facing the camera.

params.name: setting
params.desc: Sets the always_face_camera behavior to true or false.

returns.desc: status - the status of the always_face_camera behavior.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
behavior = model.definitions[0].behavior
status = behavior.always_face_camera = false

methods.name: always_face_camera?
methods.summary: The always_face_camera? method is used to retrieve the always_face_camera behavior for a component. If the always_face_camera behavior is true, then a component will always try to orient itself so that the -Y axis of the component is facing the camera.

returns.desc: behavior - true if the component is set to always face the camera, false if the component is not set to always face camera.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
# Returns a DefinitionList
definitions = model.definitions
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
definition = definitions.load path
behavior = definition.behavior
b = behavior.always_face_camera?
if (b)
  puts "Component faces camera"
else
  puts "Component does not face camera"
end
status = behavior.always_face_camera = true
b = behavior.always_face_camera?
if (b)
  puts "Alwas Face Camera is equal to true"
else
  puts "Failure"
end

methods.name: cuts_opening=
methods.summary: The cuts_opening= method is used to set the cut opening behavior for a component.

params.name: setting
params.desc: Sets the cuts_opening behavior to true or false.

returns.desc: status - the status of the cuts_opening behavior (either true or false)

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
behavior = model.definitions[0].behavior
behavior.cuts_opening = false
notes: To enable cut opening, also set #is2d= to true.

methods.name: cuts_opening?
methods.summary: The cuts_opening? method is used to get the status of a component's cut opening behavior.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
behavior = model.definitions[0].behavior
status = behavior.cuts_opening?

methods.name: is2d=
methods.summary: The #is2d= method is used to set whether the component can glue to other entities or not.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
behavior = model.definitions[0].behavior
behavior.is2d = false

methods.name: is2d?
methods.summary: The #is2d? method is used to get whether the component can glue to other entities or not.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
behavior = model.definitions[0].behavior
if behavior.is2d?
  # We can also set what planes component can glue to.
  behavior.snapto = SnapTo_Arbitrary
end

methods.name: no_scale_mask=
methods.summary: Sets an integer that is really a bit-by-bit description of which scale tool handles are hidden on a given component. This is useful for creating definitions that can only be scaled in particular ways. If a bit contains a a 1, then a certain handle set will be hidden when the user selects the component and activates the Scale tool. Here is the map of which bits control which handles.

params.name: scale_mask
params.desc: An integer describing which scale tool handles are hidden.

returns.desc: behavior - the Behavior object

methods.example:
# Disable the green and red-axes handles by setting bits 1 and 2 to 1.
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
behavior = definition.behavior
behavior.no_scale_mask = (1 << 1) + (1 << 2)

methods.name: no_scale_mask?
methods.summary: The no_scale_mask? method returns an integer that is a bit-by-bit description of which scale tool handles are hidden when the user selects this single component with the scale tool. See the no_scale_mask= method for details on the bit encodings used.

returns.desc: scale_mask - an integer describing which scale tool handles are hidden.

methods.example:
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
behavior = definition.behavior
no_scale_mask = behavior.no_scale_mask?

methods.name: shadows_face_sun=
methods.summary: The shadows_face_sun= method is used to identify whether the component's shadow will be cast from the component's current position as though the component were facing the sun. See the Component entity within the SketchUp User's guide for more information on this feature.

params.name: status
params.desc: true if the component's is to be cast from the component's current position as though the component were facing the sun. False to cause the shadow to be cast from the component's current position.

returns.desc: behavior - the Behavior object

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
behavior = model.definitions[0].behavior
behavior = behavior.shadows_face_sun = true

methods.name: shadows_face_sun?
methods.summary: The shadows_face_sun? method is used to determine whether the component's shadow is being cast from the component's current position (as though the component were facing the sun). See the Component entity within the SketchUp User's guide for more information on this feature.

returns.desc: status - true if the component's is to be cast from the component's current position as though the component were facing the sun. False to cause the shadow to be cast from the component's current position.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
# Returns a DefinitionList
definitions = model.definitions
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
begin
  definition = definitions.load path
rescue => exception
  puts exception.message
end

methods.name: snapto
methods.summary: The #snapto method is used to see how a component can glue to other entities. Returns a value indicating the snapping behavior of the component. Snapping behavior is how the x-y plane of a component instance will be snapped against a face. Possible values are:
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
behavior = model.definitions[0].behavior
snapto = behavior.snapto

methods.name: snapto=
methods.summary: The #snapto= method is used to set how a component can glue to other entities. Snapping behavior is how the x-y plane of a component instance will be snapped against a face. Possible constant values are:
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
behavior = model.definitions[0].behavior
behavior.is2d = true
behavior.snapto = SnapTo_Horizontal
notes: To enable gluing, also set #is2d= to true.
To disable gluing, set #is2d= to false.

Sketchup::Camera.summary: The Camera class contains methods for creating and manipulating a camera. The camera in SketchUp is the "point of view" from which you look at the model.

methods.name: aspect_ratio
methods.summary: Instance Methods The #aspect_ratio method is used to retrieve the aspect ratio of the Camera. `0.0` is the default value and denotes an aspect ratio matching that of the View.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup.active_model.active_view.camera
aspect_ratio = camera.aspect_ratio

methods.name: aspect_ratio=
methods.summary: The #aspect_ratio= method is used to set the aspect ratio for a Camera. Changing this value will cause SketchUp to show gray bars over the screen to show the resulting view. If you set the value to `0.0`, then the aspect ratio of the Camera will match the aspect ratio of its View.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
camera.aspect_ratio = 1.85

methods.name: center_2d
methods.summary: The #center_2d method returns a point with the x and y offset of the camera when it's in two-point perspective or math photo mode. When the camera is in two-point perspective and the user pans around, the x and y values will change. These values are in normalized device coordinates, so for instance, the range [-1.0, 1.0] spans the full width or height of the screen. The z value is unused and it is always zero.
methods.example: Sketchup.active_model.active_view.camera.center_2d

methods.name: description
methods.summary: The #description method is used to retrieve the description for a Camera.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
description = camera.description

methods.name: description=
methods.summary: The #description= method is used to set the description for the Camera.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
description = camera.description = "35 mm Camera"

methods.name: direction
methods.summary: The #direction method is used to retrieve a Vector3d object in the direction that the Camera is pointing.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
direction = camera.direction

methods.name: eye
methods.summary: The #eye method is used to retrieve the eye Point3d object for the Camera.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
eye = camera.eye

methods.name: focal_length
methods.summary: The focal_length method is used to get the focal length in millimeters of perspective Camera. This value is computed on the fly based on the camera #fov value and the camera #image_width value.
methods.example:
# Calculate focal length based on camera's current #image_width.
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
focal_length = camera.focal_length

# If you want the 35 mm focal length equivalent, a common measurement of
# camera field of view, you can instead calculate it from the #fov angle.
camera = Sketchup.active_model.active_view.camera
focal_length_35_eqv = 36.0 / (2 * Math.tan(camera.fov.degrees / 2))

methods.name: focal_length=
methods.summary: The #focal_length= method allows you to set the field of view by specifying a focal length in millimeters. Focal length must be between 1 and 3000, inclusive. The camera #fov value is set based on the provided focal_length and the current #image_width for the camera.
methods.example:
# Set field of view from focal length using camera's current #image_width.
camera = Sketchup.active_model.active_view.camera
camera.focal_length = 120

# If you instead want to set the 35 mm focal length equivalent, a common
# measurement of camera field of view, you can first convert it to an angle
# and use #fov=.
camera = Sketchup.active_model.active_view.camera
focal_length_35_eqv = 120
camera.fov = 2 * Math.atan(36.0 / (2 * focal_length_35_eqv)).radians

methods.name: fov
methods.summary: The #fov method retrieves the field of view of the Camera. This is only applicable to perspective cameras.

returns.desc: Field of view in degrees

methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
fov = camera.fov

methods.name: fov=
methods.summary: The #fov= method sets the field of view for a Camera. Field of view must be between 1 and 120 degrees, inclusive. This is only valid on a perspective camera.

params.name: fov
params.desc: Field of view in degrees

methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
fov = camera.fov = 56.78

methods.name: fov_is_height?
methods.summary: The #fov_is_height? method indicates whether the field of view is measured vertically, as opposed horizontally.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup.active_model.active_view.camera
if camera.fov_is_height?
  fov_vertical = camera.fov
  # Compute the horizontal FOV.
else
  fov_horizontal = camera.fov
  # Compute the vertical FOV.
end

methods.name: height
methods.summary: The #height method retrieves the height of a Camera. This is only valid if it is not a perspective camera.

returns.desc: height in inches.

methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
camera.perspective = false
height = camera.height

methods.name: height=
methods.summary: The #height= method is used to set the height for the Camera in inches. This is only valid if it is not a perspective camera.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
camera.perspective = false
camera.height = 20

methods.name: image_width
methods.summary: The #image_width method returns the width of the image, as used to calculate the #focal_length. This value has no effect on how the view is displayed in SketchUp. The default value, 0, is interpreted by SketchUp as 36 mm (the width of traditional 35 mm film).

returns.desc: Width in mm.

methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
width = camera.image_width

methods.name: image_width=
methods.summary: The #image_width= method is used to set the width of the image, as used to calculate the #focal_length. This value has no effect on how the view is displayed in SketchUp. The default value, 0, is interpreted by SketchUp as 36 mm (the width of traditional 35 mm film).

params.name: image_width
params.desc: Width in mm.

methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
camera.image_width = 1.0
focal_length = camera.focal_length

methods.name: initialize
signatures: initialize(eye, target, up, perspective = true, fov = 30.0)
methods.summary: Returns a new camera with eye (where the camera is) and targets (where the camera is looking).

params.name: eye
params.desc: See #eye.

params.name: target
params.desc: See #target.

params.name: up
params.desc: See #up.

params.name: perspective
params.desc: see #perspective?.

params.name: fov
params.desc: see #fov.

methods.example:
eye = Geom::Point3d.new(20, 5, 30)
target = Geom::Point3d.new(20, 60, 25)
up = Z_AXIS
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new(eye, target, up)

methods.name: is_2d?
methods.summary: The #is_2d? method indicates whether the camera mode is two-point perspective or match photo mode, as opposed to a normal perspective or parallel projection camera.
methods.example: Sketchup.active_model.active_view.camera.is_2d?

methods.name: perspective=
methods.summary: The #perspective= method is used to set whether or not this is a perspective camera or an orthographic camera.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
camera.perspective = false

methods.name: perspective?
methods.summary: The #perspective? method is used to determine whether a camera is a perspective or orthographic camera.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
status = camera.perspective?
if (status)
  puts "Perspective"
else
  puts "Orthographic"
end

methods.name: scale_2d
methods.summary: The #scale_2d method returns a float indicating the scaling factor of 2 point perspective cameras. When the camera is in two-point perspective and the user uses the zoom tools, this value will change. Zooming out will produce a value greater than 1.0.
methods.example: Sketchup.active_model.active_view.camera.scale_2d

methods.name: set
methods.summary: The #set method sets the camera orientation. You have to set the camera eye, target and up parameters at the same time to make sure that you have a valid camera definition.

params.name: eye
params.desc: See #eye.

params.name: target
params.desc: See #target.

params.name: up
params.desc: See #up.

methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
eye = Geom::Point3d.new(20, 5, 30)
target = Geom::Point3d.new(20, 60, 25)
up = Z_AXIS
camera.set(eye, target, up)

methods.name: target
methods.summary: The #target method retrieves Point3d that the camera is pointing at.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
target = camera.target

methods.name: up
methods.summary: The #up method is used to retrieve the up vector for the camera. This is the direction that the top of the camera is facing.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
up = camera.up

methods.name: xaxis
methods.summary: The #xaxis method is used to retrieve the x axis of the camera coordinate system. This value is computed from the cross product between the camera direction and the up vector.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
xaxis = camera.xaxis

methods.name: yaxis
methods.summary: The #yaxis method retrieves the y axis of the camera coordinate system. This value is computed to be perpendicular the camera x and z axes. It is equivalent to the up direction, but is computed to make sure that it is perpendicular to the direction.
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
# 0.0, 1.0, 0.0
yaxis = camera.yaxis

methods.name: zaxis
methods.summary: The #zaxis method retrieves the z axis of the camera coordinate system. This value is computed. It is the same as Camera.direction
methods.example:
camera = Sketchup::Camera.new
# 0.0, 1.0, 0.0
vector = camera.zaxis

Sketchup::ClassificationSchema.summary: The ClassificationSchema class represent schemas loaded in the model.

methods.summary: Instance Methods The <=> method is used to compare two ClassificationSchema objects for sorting. The comparison is done based on the schema name.

params.name: schema2
params.desc: The second schema in the comparison.

returns.desc: Integer - -1 if schema1 is less then schema2. 1 if schema1 is greater than schema2, 0 if the schemas are equal.

methods.example:
schema1 = Sketchup.active_model.classifications["IFC 2x3"]
schema2 = Sketchup.active_model.classifications["gbXML"]
# Returns -1
result = schema1 <=> schema2
# Returns an array of sorted schemas.
schemas = Sketchup.active_model.classifications.to_a.sort

methods.name: name
methods.summary: The name method returns the name of the schema.

returns.desc: String - containing the schema name.

methods.name: namespace
methods.summary: The namespace method returns the namespace of the schema.

returns.desc: String - containing the schema namespace.

Sketchup::Classifications.summary: The Classifications class is a container/manager for all classifications in a model.

methods.summary: Instance Methods The [] method is used to get a classification schema by name or index.

params.name: index_or_name
params.desc: The index or name of the ClassificationSchema object.

returns.desc: schema - a ClassificationSchema object if successful, otherwise nil.

methods.example:
# Get schema by name:
schema = Sketchup.active_model.classifications["IFC 2x3"]

# Get schema by index:
schema = Sketchup.active_model.classifications[1]

methods.name: each
methods.summary: The #each method is used to iterate through loaded classification schemas.

methods.name: keys
methods.summary: The keys method is used to get a list of keys in the Classifications class, which are the same as the names of the schemas.

returns.desc: keys - Array of string keys

methods.example: schema_names = Sketchup.active_model.classifications.keys

methods.name: length
methods.summary: The #length method returns the number of loaded classification schemas.
methods.example: Sketchup.active_model.classifications.length

methods.name: load_schema
methods.summary: The load_schema method is used to load a classification schema into a model.

params.name: file
params.desc: Full path to the schema file

returns.desc: True if successful.

methods.example:
c = Sketchup.active_model.classifications
file = Sketchup.find_support_file('IFC4.skc', 'Classifications')
status = c.load_schema(file) if !file.nil?

methods.name: size
methods.summary: The #size method returns the number of loaded classification schemas.
methods.example: Sketchup.active_model.classifications.size

methods.name: unload_schema
methods.summary: The unload_schema method is used to unload a classification schema that was previously loaded into a model.

params.name: schema_name
params.desc: Name of the schema to unload

returns.desc: True if successful.

methods.example:
c = Sketchup.active_model.classifications
status = c.unload_schema('IFC 2x3')

Sketchup::Color.summary: The Color class is used to create and manipulate colors within SketchUp Models. The class can also be used the same way with LayOut documents. For methods that accept a Color object, such as the face.material method, you can pass in an actual Color object, or an object that can be converted to a Color. For example:

methods.name: names
methods.summary: Class Methods The .names method is used to retrieve an array of all color names recognized by SketchUp. In general, whenever a method wants a color, you can pass in a String with one of these names.
methods.example: array = Sketchup::Color.names

methods.summary: Instance Methods The #== method checks to see if the two Sketchup::Colors are equal. This checks whether the RGBA values are the same. In versions prior to SketchUp 2018 two color objects with the same values would be considered different.
methods.example: SketchUp::Color.new(255, 255, 255) == Sketchup::Color.new(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)

methods.name: alpha
methods.summary: The #alpha method is used to retrieve the opacity of the color. A value of 0 is transparent, 255 is opaque.
methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "OldLace"
alpha = color.alpha

methods.name: alpha=
methods.summary: The #alpha= method is used to set the opacity of the color. A value of 0 is transparent, 255 is opaque.

params.name: alpha
params.desc: The new opacity value.

methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
alpha = color.alpha = 255

methods.name: blend
methods.summary: The #blend method is used to blend two colors. The blended color will be the result of taking (1 - weight) * color1 + weight * color2. If weight = 0, you will get color2. If weight = 1 you will get color1.

params.name: color2
params.desc: The second color to be blended (with this color).

params.name: weight
params.desc: A Float between 0.0 and 1.0

methods.example:
color1 = Sketchup::Color.new "OldLace"
color2 = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
color3 = color1.blend color2, 0.5

methods.name: blue
methods.summary: The #blue method is used to retrieve the blue value of a color. Value range is 0 to 255.
methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
blue = color.blue

methods.name: blue=
methods.summary: The #blue= method is used to set the blue value of a color. Value range is 0 to 255.

params.name: blue
params.desc: The blue value for the color.

methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
blue = color.blue = 200

methods.name: green
methods.summary: The #green method is used to retrieve the green value of a color. Value range is 0 to 255.
methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
green = color.green

methods.name: green=
methods.summary: The #green= method is used to set the green component of a RGB Color. Value range is 0 to 255.

params.name: green
params.desc: The green value for the color.

methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
green = color.green = 200

methods.name: initialize
methods.summary: The new method is used to create a new Color object.

params.name: red
params.desc: A red value between 0 and 255.

params.name: green
params.desc: A green value between 0 and 255.

params.name: blue
params.desc: A blue value between 0 and 255.

params.name: alpha
params.desc: A alpha value between 0 and 255.

params.name: name
params.desc: A string name of a color that currently exists in SketchUp. See the table at the start of this class description for more info.

params.name: hex
params.desc: A hexadecimal color code.

methods.example:
color_from_name = Sketchup::Color.new "OldLace"
color_from_rgb = Sketchup::Color.new(0, 128, 255)
color_from_rgba = Sketchup::Color.new(0, 128, 255, 128)
color_from_hex = Sketchup::Color.new(0xFF0000)

# You can then assign colors to the material of DrawingElements.
# Note that this creates a new Material object, and the alpha value
# of the color does NOT get applied to the new Material. You must
# manually set the alpha to get transparent materials.
face.material = color_from_rgba
face.material.alpha = 0.5
notes: When assigning colors via a hexadecimal, R and B will be flipped.
When assigning colors via a hexadecimal, Alpha is not supported.

methods.name: red
methods.summary: The #red method is used to retrieve the red component of a RGB Color. Value range is 0 to 255.
methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
red = color.red

methods.name: red=
methods.summary: The #red= method is used to set the red component of a RGB Color. Value range is 0 to 255.

params.name: red
params.desc: The red value for the color.

methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
red = color.red=200

methods.name: to_a
methods.summary: The #to_a method is used to convert a Color object to an Array object. The returned array will contain 4 integer values (RGBA) between 0 and 255.
methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
color_array = color.to_a

methods.name: to_i
methods.summary: The #to_i method is used to convert a Color object to an 32 bit integer.
methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new "AliceBlue"
integer = color.to_i

methods.name: to_s
methods.summary: The #to_s method returns a string representation of the Sketchup::Color object, in the form of "Color(255, 255, 255, 255)".
methods.example:
color = Sketchup::Color.new(255, 255, 255, 255)
color_str = color.to_s

Sketchup::ComponentDefinition.summary: The Sketchup::ComponentDefinition class is used to define the contents for a SketchUp component. Components are a collection of entities that can be instanced and reused multiple times throughout a model. For example, you could draw a chair once, turn it into a component, and then use 6 instances of it to surround a table. Edits to the original "definition" will then propagate across all of its instances.

methods.summary: Instance Methods The <=> method is used to compare two ComponentDefinition objects for sorting. The comparison is done based on the component name.

params.name: compdef2
params.desc: The second component definition in the comparison.

returns.desc: a -1 if component1 is less then component2. A 1 if component1 greater than component2

methods.example:
c1=Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
c2=Sketchup.find_support_file "Fence.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
if c1 <=> c2
  puts "c1 sorts before c2"
end

methods.summary: The == method is used to test if two ComponentDefinition objects are the same (based on their address in memory).

params.name: compdef2
params.desc: The second component definition in the comparison.

returns.desc: true if the ComponentDefinition objects are the same object. False if the objects are not the same.

methods.example:
c1=Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
c2=Sketchup.find_support_file "Fence.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
c1 == c2

methods.name: add_classification
methods.summary: The add_classification method is used to add a given classification to the component. Note that you cannot classify image definitions.

params.name: schema_name
params.desc: a String - Schema name to add

params.name: schema_type
params.desc: a String - Schema type to add

returns.desc: true if the classification succeeds. Otherwise false.

methods.example:
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions.first
success = definition.add_classification("IFC 2x3", "IfcDoor")

methods.name: add_observer
methods.summary: The add_observer method is used to add an observer to the current object.

params.name: observer
params.desc: An observer.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
status = componentdefinition.add_observer observer

methods.name: behavior
methods.summary: The behavior method is used to retrieve the Behavior object associated with a component definition.

returns.desc: a Behavior object if successful

methods.example:
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
model = Sketchup.active_model
definitions = model.definitions
componentdefinition = definitions.load path
behavior = componentdefinition.behavior

methods.name: count_instances
methods.summary: The count_instances method is used to count the number of unique component instances in a model using this component definition. This does not represent the total number of instances placed in the model as it doesn't take into account instances inside unused definitions.

returns.desc: the number of component instances of this component definition (if successful)

methods.example:
path = Sketchup.find_support_file('Bed.skp',
  'Components/Components Sampler/')
definitions = Sketchup.active_model.definitions
definition = definitions.load(path)
number = definition.count_instances

methods.name: count_used_instances
methods.summary: The count_used_instances method is used to count the total number of component instances in a model using this component definition. This method takes into account the full hierarchy of the model.

returns.desc: the number of component instances of this component definition (if successful)

methods.example:
path = Sketchup.find_support_file('Bed.skp',
  'Components/Components Sampler/')
definitions = Sketchup.active_model.definitions
definition = definitions.load(path)
number = definition.count_used_instances

methods.name: description
methods.summary: The description method is used to retrieve the description of the component definition. Component definitions do not have a description, by default.

returns.desc: the description of the component definition if successful

methods.example:
# Get the description
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
description = componentdefinition.description

methods.name: description=
methods.summary: The description= method is used to set the description for the component definition.

returns.desc: the description if successful, false if unsuccessful

methods.example:
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
componentdefinition.description = "This is a traditional bed"
description = componentdefinition.description

methods.name: entities
methods.summary: The entities method retrieves a collection of all the entities in the component definition

returns.desc: an Entities object if successful

methods.example:
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
entities = componentdefinition.entities

methods.name: get_classification_value
methods.summary: The get_classification_value method is used to retrieve the value from a classification attribute given a key path.

params.name: path
params.desc: An array composed of the key path to the value.

returns.desc: a Ruby object if successful, nil otherwise.

methods.example:
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions.first
definition.add_classification("IFC 2x3", "IfcDoor")

path = ["IFC 2x3", "IfcDoor", "ObjectType", "IfcLabel"]
value = definition.get_classification_value(path)

methods.name: group?
methods.summary: The group? method is used to determine if this component definition is used to hold the elements of a group.
methods.example:
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
model = Sketchup.active_model
definitions = model.definitions
componentdefinition = definitions.load path
status = componentdefinition.group?

methods.name: guid
methods.summary: The guid method is used to retrieve the unique identifier of this component definition. The guid changes after the component definition is modified and the component edit is exited.

returns.desc: a string guid if successful

methods.example:
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
guid = componentdefinition.guid

methods.name: hidden?
methods.summary: The #hidden? method is used to determine if this component definition is hidden in the component browser. This is based on how its instances are placed in the model hierarchy. For more details, see article[https://developer.sketchup.com/article-hiddensubcomponents]. In addition, component definitions used by Groups and Images are always hidden in the Component Browser. See #group? and #image?.
methods.example:
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
status = componentdefinition.hidden?

methods.name: image?
methods.summary: The image? method is used to determine if this component definition is used to define an image.
methods.example:
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
status = componentdefinition.image?

methods.name: insertion_point
methods.summary: The insertion_point method is used to retrieve the Point3d object where the component was inserted.

returns.desc: the Point3d where the component was inserted if successful. False if unsuccessful.

methods.deprecated: SketchUp 2020.0 removed the insertion point feature. The getter will always return the origin point and the setter becomes a no-op.
methods.example:
point = Geom::Point3d.new 10,20,30
transform = Geom::Transformation.new point
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
definitions = model.definitions
componentdefinition = definitions.load path
instance = entities.add_instance componentdefinition, transform
point = componentdefinition.insertion_point

methods.name: insertion_point=
methods.summary: Sets the insertion point of your definition.

params.name: point
params.desc: The Point3d object to use as the insertion point.

returns.desc: The Point3d object used as the insertion point.

methods.deprecated: SketchUp 2020.0 removed the insertion point feature. The getter will always return the origin point and the setter becomes a no-op.
methods.example:
point = Geom::Point3d.new(10, 20, 0)
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
componentdefinition.insertion_point = point

methods.name: instances
methods.summary: The instances method is used to return any array of ComponentInstancesfor this ComponentDefinition.

returns.desc: an array of ComponentInstances (if successful)

methods.example:
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
instances = componentdefinition.instances

methods.name: internal?
methods.summary: The internal? method is used to determine if the component definition is internal to the Component Browser
methods.example:
point = Geom::Point3d.new 10,20,30
transform = Geom::Transformation.new point
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
definitions = model.definitions
componentdefinition = definitions.load path
status = componentdefinition.internal?

methods.name: invalidate_bounds
methods.summary: Invalidates the bounding box of your definition. This command forces the update of the bounding box of definition while inside an operation. See Model.start_operation for how to start an operation. This method is useful if you make changes to your geometry using the Ruby API and then need to know your bounding box size. This method forces SketchUp to recalculate the definition's bounding box when you choose.

returns.desc: true if successful

methods.example:
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
componentdefinition.invalidate_bounds

methods.name: live_component?
methods.summary: The #live_component? method is used to identify Live Components and sub-definitions of Live Components.
methods.example:
Skipping Live Components
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.definitions.each { |definition|
  next if definition.live_component?
  puts definition.name
}
notes: These components are parametrically generated and API users should not modify them.

methods.name: load_time
methods.summary: The #load_time method gets the load time of the component definition. For an internal component definition, this is the time that it was created. For an external component definition, this is the time that it was added to the model.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
definition = model.definitions.first
definition.load_time

methods.name: name
methods.summary: The name method retrieves the name of the component definition.

returns.desc: the component definition's name if successful

methods.example:
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
model = Sketchup.active_model
definitions = model.definitions
componentdefinition = definitions.load path
name = componentdefinition.name

methods.name: name=
methods.summary: The name= method is used to set the name of the component definition. The name should be unique to the model, if it's not the name will automatically be made unique.
bugs: In SketchUp 2022.0 a bug might lead to an available name being incorrectly renamed. Or a name that should be unavailable would be duplicated. This was fixed in SketchUp 2022.0.1.
methods.example:
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/"
model = Sketchup.active_model
definitions = model.definitions
componentdefinition = definitions.load path
name = componentdefinition.name="Bed"

methods.name: path
methods.summary: The path method is used to retrieve the path where the component was loaded.

returns.desc: Returns empty string if it is an internal component.

methods.example:
path = Sketchup.find_support_file("Bed.skp", "Components/Components Sampler/")
model = Sketchup.active_model
definitions = model.definitions
componentdefinition = definitions.load(path)
path = componentdefinition.path

methods.name: refresh_thumbnail
methods.summary: The refresh_thumbnail method is used to force SketchUp to regenerate the thumbnail image that appears in the component browser. This is useful if you've used the API to change the geometry of your component and would like the thumbnail to match.
methods.example:
componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
componentdefinition.refresh_thumbnail

methods.name: remove_classification
methods.summary: The remove_classification method is used to remove a given classification from the component. Note that you cannot classify image definitions.

params.name: schema_name
params.desc: Schema name to remove

params.name: schema_type
params.desc: Schema type to remove. If not provided or an empty string, the currently applied schema type for the given schema name will be removed.

returns.desc: true if the removal succeeds. Otherwise false.

methods.example:
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions.first
success = definition.remove_classification("IFC 2x3", "IfcDoor")

methods.name: remove_observer

my_definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]

componentdefinition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]

Sketchup::ComponentInstance.summary: The Sketchup::ComponentInstance class is used to represent component instances of a component definition or components that have been dragged from the Component Browser and placed (thus, instanced) within the Model. Therefore, the ComponentInstance class contains a reference to a corresponding ComponentDefinition object and a Transformation object (which contains the location of the component in the Drawing Window).

methods.name: add_observer
methods.summary: Instance Methods The add_observer method is used to add an observer to the current object.

params.name: observer
params.desc: An observer.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
status = componentinstance.add_observer observer

methods.name: definition
methods.summary: The definition method is used to retrieve the component definition for this component instance.

returns.desc: a ComponentDefinition object if successful

methods.example:
# First create an instance for us to look at.
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)

# You can get an instance's definition with this method.
definition = componentinstance.definition

methods.name: definition=
methods.summary: The definition= method is used to set the component definition for this component. This method causes the instance to use a different definition, but it will use the same transformation to position it in the Model.

params.name: definition
params.desc: A ComponentDefinition object to set.

returns.desc: the ComponentDefinition object that was set if successful, false if unsuccessful

methods.example:
# Assumes that the active model contains two different components.
instance1 = Sketchup.active_model.entities[0]
instance2 = Sketchup.active_model.entities[1]

# Grab handles to our two definitions.
definition1 = instance1.definition
definition2 = instance2.definition

# Replace 2nd instance with the 1st definition.
instance2.definition = definition1

methods.name: equals?
methods.summary: The equals? method is used to determine if a component instance is geometrically equivalent to another instance.

params.name: instance
params.desc: The instance to compare this instance with.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
instance1 = entities[0]
instance2 = entities[1]
status = instance1.equals?(instance2)

methods.name: explode
methods.summary: The explode method is used to explode the component instance into separate entities.

returns.desc: An array of entity objects if successful, false if unsuccessful

methods.example:
# Assuming 'instance' is a ComponentInstance object
instance = Sketchup.active_model.active_entities.grep(Sketchup::ComponentInstance).first
entities = instance.explode

methods.name: glued_to
methods.summary: The #glued_to method is used to retrieve the entity that this instance is glued to.
methods.example:
point = Geom::Point3d.new(10, 20, 30)
transform = Geom::Transformation.new(point)
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
path = Sketchup.find_support_file("Bed.skp", "Components/Components Sampler/")
definitions = model.definitions
componentdefinition = definitions.load(path)
instance = entities.add_instance(componentdefinition, transform)
status = instance.glued_to

methods.name: glued_to=
methods.summary: The glued_to= method glues this instance to a drawing element. When moving this other drawing elment with the Move tool, the glued instance moves with it. In SketchUp 2021.1 support for passing Sketchup::Group, Sketchup::ComponentInstance and Sketchup::Image was added.

returns.desc: the entity the instance was glued to.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities

# Create a face
face = entities.add_face([[0, 0, 0], [100, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0], [0, 100, 0]])

# Add component
path = Sketchup.find_support_file("Bed.skp", "Components/Components Sampler/")
point = Geom::Point3d.new(10, 10, 0)
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new(point)
definitions = model.definitions
definition = definitions.load(path)
instance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)

# Make component "gluable"
definition.behavior.is2d = true

# Glue the component to the face.
# If you now move the face, the component will follow.
instance.glued_to = face
raises: ArgumentError if the Sketchup::Behavior for this component doesn't allow gluing, if the alignment is wrong, or if this would lead to cyclic gluing.

methods.name: guid
methods.summary: The guid method is used to get the base 64 encoded unique id for this SketchUp object.

returns.desc: a unique 22 character string

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)

methods.name: intersect
methods.summary: The intersect method is used to compute the boolean intersection of two instances representing manifold solid volumes (this - arg). If the specified objects (this and arg) do not represent manifold volumes, this method fails.

params.name: instance
params.desc: The instance to intersect this instance with.

returns.desc: The resultant group if the two objects (this and arg) represent manifold solids and the operation succeeds otherwise nil is returned.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
instance1 = entities[0]
instance2 = entities[1]
result = instance1.intersect(instance2)
notes: This method is not available in SketchUp Make.

methods.name: locked=
methods.summary: The locked= method is used to lock a component instance.

returns.desc: true if the component instance is locked. False if the instance is not locked.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
status = componentinstance.locked = true

methods.name: locked?
methods.summary: The locked? method is used to determine if a component instance is locked.
methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
status = componentinstance.locked?

methods.name: make_unique
methods.summary: The #make_unique method is used to create a component definition for this instance that is not used by any other instances. If the component is already unique in the model, nothing happens.

returns.desc: returns itself

methods.example:
point = Geom::Point3d.new(10,20,30)
transform = Geom::Transformation.new(point)
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities

path = Sketchup.find_support_file("Bed.skp",
  "Components/Components Sampler/")
definitions = model.definitions
componentdefinition = definitions.load(path)
instance = entities.add_instance(componentdefinition, transform)
# Returns unique component instance
instance.make_unique

methods.name: manifold?
methods.summary: The manifold? method is used to determine if an instance is manifold.
methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
status = componentinstance.manifold?

methods.name: move!
methods.summary: The #move! method is used to set the transformation of this component instance, similarly to #transformation= but without recording to the undo stack. This method is useful for moving entities inside of an animation or page transition.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
new_transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([100,0,0])
componentinstance.move!(new_transformation)
notes: Despite the name being similar to #transform!, this method closer corresponds to #transformation=.

methods.name: name
methods.summary: The name method is used to get the name of this instance.

returns.desc: the string name of the ComponentInstance

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
name = componentinstance.name

methods.name: name=
methods.summary: The name method is used to set the name of this instance.

params.name: name
params.desc: the string name to set

returns.desc: the newly named ComponentInstance

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
componentinstance.name = "Sang"

methods.name: outer_shell
methods.summary: The outer_shell method is used to compute the outer shell of the two instances representing manifold solid volumes (this || arg). If the specified objects (this and arg) do not represent manifold volumes, this method fails.

params.name: instance
params.desc: The instance to outer shell this instance with.

returns.desc: The resultant group if the two objects (this and arg) represent manifold solids and the operation succeeds otherwise nil is returned.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
instance1 = entities[0]
instance2 = entities[1]
result = instance1.outer_shell(instance2)

methods.name: remove_observer
methods.summary: The remove_observer method is used to remove an observer from the current object.

params.name: observer
params.desc: An observer.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
status = componentinstance.remove_observer observer

methods.name: show_differences
methods.summary: The show_differences method is used to determine if a component instance is geometrically equivalent to another instance and in addition move the non- matching and matching geometry to new layers.

params.name: instance
params.desc: The instance to be compared with.

params.name: verbose
params.desc: A boolean flag indicating whether to display a textural report of the found differences to the Ruby console.

returns.desc: true if the instances are geometrically equivalent, otherwise false.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
instance1 = entities[0]
instance2 = entities[1]
status = instance1.show_differences(instance2, true)

methods.name: split
methods.summary: The split method is used to compute the boolean split (map overlay)of the two instances representing manifold solid volumes (this - arg). If the specified objects (this and arg) do not represent manifold volumes, this method fails.

params.name: instance
params.desc: The instance to split this instance with.

returns.desc: A vector (array) of the three

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
instance1 = entities[0]
instance2 = entities[1]
result = instance1.split(instance2)

methods.name: subtract
methods.summary: The subtract method is used to compute the boolean difference of the two instances representing manifold solid volumes (this - arg). If the specified objects (this and arg) do not represent manifold volumes, this method fails.

params.name: instance
params.desc: The instance to subtract this instance from.

returns.desc: The resultant group if the two objects (this and arg) represent manifold solids and the operation succeeds otherwise nil is returned.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
instance1 = entities[0]
instance2 = entities[1]
result = instance1.subtract(instance2)
notes: This method is not available in SketchUp Make.

methods.name: transform!
methods.summary: Apply a Geom::Transformation to a component instance.

params.name: transform
params.desc: The transformation object to apply to the component instance.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0, 0, 0])

new_transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([100, 0, 0])

methods.name: transformation
methods.summary: The transformation method is used to retrieve the transformation of this instance.

returns.desc: the Transformation object if successful

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
t = componentinstance.transformation

methods.name: transformation=
methods.summary: The #transformation= method is used to set the transformation of this component instance.
methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]

new_transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([100,0,0])
componentinstance.transformation = new_transformation
notes: As of SketchUp 2026, this will raise an error if the Geom::Transformation is not invertible. Prior to 2026 this would silently set the transformation possibly causing rendering or editing problems.
raises: ArgumentError if the Geom::Transformation is not invertible (as of Sketchup 2026)

methods.name: trim
methods.summary: The #trim method is used to compute the (non-destructive) boolean difference of the two instances representing manifold solid volumes (this - arg). If the specified objects (this and arg) do not represent manifold volumes, this method fails.

params.name: instance
params.desc: The instance to trim this instance against.

returns.desc: The resultant group if the two objects (this and arg) represent manifold solids and the operation succeeds otherwise nil is returned.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
instance1 = entities[0]
instance2 = entities[1]
result = instance1.trim(instance2)
notes: Trimming object instance2 using instance1 results in a new trimmed version of instance2. If the trim is successful the original instance2 is erased and a newly trimmed version is created. This new ...
This method is not available in SketchUp Make.

methods.name: union
methods.summary: The union method is used to compute the boolean union of the two instances representing manifold solid volumes (this | arg). If the specified objects (this and arg) do not represent manifold volumes, this method fails.

params.name: instance
params.desc: The instance to union this instance with.

returns.desc: The resultant group if the two objects (this and arg) represent manifold solids and the operation succeeds otherwise nil is returned.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
instance1 = entities[0]
instance2 = entities[1]
result = instance1.union(instance2)
notes: This method is not available in SketchUp Make.

methods.name: volume
