methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
definition = Sketchup.active_model.definitions[0]
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([0,0,0])
componentinstance = entities.add_instance(definition, transformation)
volume = componentinstance.volume

Sketchup::Console.summary: The Console class is used by SketchUp to direct $stdout and $stderr to the Ruby Console. It is a singleton class that only has one instance available. This instance is accessible via the SKETCHUP_CONSOLE constant. In SketchUp 2014 methods were added to allow developers to control the visibility of the Ruby Console.

methods.name: clear
methods.summary: Instance Methods Clears the contents of SketchUp's Ruby Console.

returns.desc: true.

methods.example: SKETCHUP_CONSOLE.clear

methods.name: hide
methods.summary: Hides the SketchUp Ruby Console.

returns.desc: true.

methods.example: SKETCHUP_CONSOLE.hide

methods.name: show
methods.summary: Displays the SketchUp Ruby Console.

returns.desc: true.

methods.example: SKETCHUP_CONSOLE.show

methods.name: visible?
methods.summary: Returns the visibility state of the SketchUp Ruby Console.

returns.desc: true if visible, false if not.

methods.example: puts SKETCHUP_CONSOLE.visible?

Sketchup::ConstructionLine.summary: The ConstructionLine class contains methods for modifying construction lines. Construction lines can be infinite in length, semi-infinite (i.e. infinite in one direction) or finite.

methods.name: direction
methods.summary: Instance Methods The direction method retrieves a 3D vector in the direction of the construction line.

returns.desc: vector - a Vector3d object if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0,0,0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(20,20,20)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, point2)
vector = constline.direction

methods.name: direction=
methods.summary: The direction= method is used to set the direction of the construction line to a 3D vector.

params.name: vector
params.desc: The Vector3d whose direction will be used to set the direction of the construction line.

returns.desc: vector - the new Vector3d object if successful

methods.example:
# Draw a construction line that points diagonally.
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
constline = entities.add_cline([10,10,10], [200,200,200])

# Create a new direction that is straight up, and redirect the line.
new_direction = [0, 0, 1]
constline.direction = new_direction

methods.name: end
methods.summary: The end method retrieves the end point of a construction line in the form of a 3D point. If the construction line is infinite at the end, this returns nil.

returns.desc: point - a Point3d object representing the end of the construction line

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0,0,0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(20,20,20)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, point2)
endofline = constline.end

methods.name: end=
methods.summary: The end= method is used to set the end point of the construction line. This method will make the length finite at the end. Set the end to nil to make the construction line infinite at the end.

params.name: point
params.desc: The Point3d object to set for the end point of the construction line.

params.name: nil
params.desc: Sets the end point to infinite.

returns.desc: point - a Point3d object if successful or nil

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(20, 20, 20)
point3 = Geom::Point3d.new(10, 10, 10)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, point2)
constline.end = point3
# Will shorten the line to [10, 10, 10]

methods.name: position
methods.summary: The position method is used to retrieve a 3D point used to create a construction line on an infinite construction line.

returns.desc: point - the Point3d object used to create the line (if successful)

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0,0,0)
vector = Geom::Vector3d.new(10,10,10)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, vector)
# Returns point1 or 0,0,0
position = constline.position

methods.name: position=
methods.summary: The position= method is used to set a 3D point that the construction passes through

params.name: point
params.desc: The Point3d object for the construction line to pass through.

returns.desc: point - the new Point3d object that the construction line will pass through (if successful)

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0,0,0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(20,20,20)
point3 = Geom::Point3d.new(0,20,20)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, point2)
position = constline.position = point3

methods.name: reverse!
methods.summary: The reverse! method is used to reverse the direction of the construction line.

returns.desc: status

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0,0,0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(20,20,20)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, point2)
status = constline.reverse!

methods.name: start
methods.summary: The start method is used to retrieve the starting point of a construction line. If the construction line is infinite at the start, this returns nil.

returns.desc: point - the Poin3d object representing the starting point of the construction line (if successful)

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0,0,0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(20,20,20)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, point2)
startofline = constline.start

methods.name: start=
methods.summary: The start= method is used to set the start point of a construction line making the line's length finite at the start. Setting the start to nil will make the construction line infinite at the start.

params.name: point
params.desc: The Point3d object to set for the start point of the construction line.

params.name: nil
params.desc: Sets the start point to infinite.

returns.desc: point - a Point3d object if successful or nil

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0,0,0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(20,20,20)
point3 = Geom::Point3d.new(5,5,5)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, point2)
startofline = constline.start = point3

methods.name: stipple
methods.summary: The #stipple method is used to retrieve the stipple pattern used to display the construction line.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(20, 20, 20)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, point2)
puts constline.stipple

methods.name: stipple=
methods.summary: The #stipple= method is used to set the stipple pattern used to display the construction line. The stipple pattern is given as a string. Valid strings are: - "." (Dotted Line), - "-" (Short Dashes Line), - "_" (Long Dashes Line), - "-.-" (Dash Dot Dash Line).
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(20, 20, 20)
constline = entities.add_cline(point1, point2)
constline.stipple = "-.-"

Sketchup::ConstructionPoint.summary: A construction point represents a point in the model that can be used to aid in other modeling operations. For example, you may put a construction point at the center of a circle to make it easier to locate that point for performing other operations.

model = Sketchup.active_model

Sketchup::Curve.summary: The Curve class is used by SketchUp to unite a series of Edge objects into one conceptual entity. Since SketchUp is a surface modeler, all circles, arcs, and arbitrary curves are really just edges that are bound together in sequence.

methods.name: count_edges
methods.summary: Instance Methods The count_edges method is used to retrieve the number of Edge objects that make up the Curve.

returns.desc: num_edges - the number of edges in the curve

methods.example:
centerpoint = Geom::Point3d.new
# Create a circle perpendicular to the normal or Z axis
vector = Geom::Vector3d.new 0,0,1

# get the path (instance_path, point)

point2 = point2.transform(new_instance_path.transformation.inverse)

Sketchup::Drawingelement.summary: Drawingelement is a base class for an item in the model that can be displayed. These items include edges, construction points, construction lines, and images. methods.name: bounds

pts[3] = [0, depth, 0]

methods.name: erase!
methods.summary: The #erase! method is used to erase an element from the model. Erasing an Edge also erases all of the Face objects that use the Edge.
bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2023.0 this could crash SketchUp if you erased an instance used by the active edit path.

width = 100

Sketchup::Edge.summary: The Edge class contains methods modifying and extracting information for edges.

methods.name: all_connected
methods.summary: Instance Methods The all_connected method retrieves all of the entities connected to an edge, including the edge itself.

returns.desc: the edge and entities connected to that edge

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
points = [
  Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(100, 0, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(100, 100, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(200, 100, 0)
]
# Add the edges to the model
edges = entities.add_edges(points)
connected_entities = edges.first.all_connected

methods.name: common_face
methods.summary: The common_face method is used to identify a face that is common to two edges.

params.name: edge2
params.desc: The face whose edge you are checking for commonality.

returns.desc: the Face object that is common to the two edges if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
points = [
  Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(100, 0, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(100, 100, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(0, 100, 0)
]
# Add the face to the entities in the model
face = entities.add_face(points)
edge1 = face.edges[0]
edge2 = face.edges[1]
face = edge1.common_face(edge2)

methods.name: curve
methods.summary: The curve method is used to get the Curve object that this edge belongs to, if any. Note that if the edge is part of an arc instead of a random curve, then this method will return an ArcCurve object.

returns.desc: returns a Curve object if it is a curve, nil if it is not a curve

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
edges = entities.add_curve([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0], [100, 200, 0])
curve = edges[0].curve

methods.name: end
methods.summary: The end method is used to retrieve the Vertex object at the end of the edge.

returns.desc: a Vertex object if successful

methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
vertex = edge.end

methods.name: explode_curve
methods.summary: The explode_curve method is used to explode the curve that the given edge is a part of.

returns.desc: an exploded edge object if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
edges = entities.add_curve([0, 0, 0], [100, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
edge = edges[0]
exploded_edge = edge.explode_curve

methods.name: faces
methods.summary: The #faces method is used to retrieve all of the faces common to the edge.
methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
faces = edge.faces

methods.name: find_faces
methods.summary: The find_faces method is used to create all of the Faces that can be created with this edge. For example, if you use the API to draw three edges that form a triangle, the face between them will not show up because you've only drawn the edges, but if you call find_faces on one of the edges, the triangle will be filled in.

returns.desc: the number of faces found

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
points = [
  Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(100, 0, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(100, 100, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(0, 100, 0),
  Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
]
edges = entities.add_curve(points)
number_of_faces_found = edges[0].find_faces

methods.name: length
methods.summary: The #length method is used to retrieve the length of an edge in current units.

params.name: transform
params.desc: A Transformation object or array that can be interpreted as a Transformation object.

returns.desc: the length of the edge

methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
edge.length

methods.name: line
methods.summary: The line method is used to retrieve the line defined by the edge. Lines in SketchUp aren't visible entities but geometric constructs represented by an Array with a Point3d and a Vector3d. See the Geom module and the Array class for more information on lines.

returns.desc: an array with a Point3d object and a Vector3d object.

methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0,0,0], [100, 100, 0])
line = edge.line

methods.name: other_vertex
methods.summary: The other_vertex method is used to find the opposite vertex given one vertex of the edge.

params.name: vertex1
params.desc: One of the Vertex objects associated with the edge.

returns.desc: the other Vertex object associated with the edge

methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0],[100, 100, 0])
# Get the end vertex of an edge
vertex = edge.end
# Should find the starting vertex
other_vertex = edge.other_vertex(vertex)

methods.name: reversed_in?
methods.summary: The #reversed_in? method is used to determine if the edge is reversed in a face's bounding loop.

params.name: face
params.desc: The face that is bounded by the edge.

returns.desc: true if the edge is reversed, false if it is not reversed. nil if the edge and face is not connected.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
points = []
points[0] = [0, 0, 0]
points[1] = [9, 0, 0]
points[2] = [9, 9, 0]
points[3] = [0, 9, 0]
# Add the face to the entities in the model.
face = entities.add_face(points)
edge = face.edges[0]
edge.reversed_in?(face)

methods.name: smooth=
methods.summary: The #smooth= method is used to set the edge to be smooth. A smooth edge will cause the shading between connected faces to blend to a smooth transition. The edge will still be visible.
methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
edge.soft = true
edge.smooth = true
notes: The soft and smooth properties are normally set in pairs. You can observer this when the Soften/Smooth Edges feature or holding down Ctrl when using the Eraser Tool.

methods.name: smooth?
methods.summary: The #smooth? method is used to retrieve the current smooth setting for an edge. A smooth edge will cause the shading between connected faces to blend to a smooth transition. The edge will still be visible.
methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
edge.smooth = true
edge.smooth?

methods.name: soft=
methods.summary: The #soft= method is used to set the edge to be soft. A soft edge will cause the connected faces to be treated as a surface. This means that if you have Hidden Geometry off and select one face it will also select all faces connected with soft edges. A soft edge will also appear hidden.
methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
edge.smooth = true
edge.soft = true
notes: The soft and smooth properties are normally set in pairs. You can observe this when the Soften/Smooth Edges feature or holding down Ctrl when using the Eraser Tool.

methods.name: soft?
methods.summary: The #soft? method is used to retrieve the current soft setting for an edge. A soft edge will cause the connected faces to be treated as a surface. This means that if you have Hidden Geometry off and select one face it will also select all faces connected with soft edges. A soft edge will also appear hidden.
methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
edge.soft = true
edge.soft?

methods.name: split
methods.summary: The #split method is used to split an edge into two or more distinct edges. If a Point3d is given, it must be a point that is on the Edge. If a Float is given, it is a number between 0 and 1 that gives the relative position along the edge at which to split it. For example, edge.split(0.5) will split the Edge at its midpoint. This split position is measured from the Edge.start.

params.name: position
params.desc: A Point3d object whose location is along the edge, or a Float between 0.0 and 1.0 defining how far along the edge to split.

returns.desc: the new Edge object that was split off the old one if successful

methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
new_edge = edge.split(0.5)

methods.name: start
methods.summary: The start method is used to retrieve the Vertex object at the start of the edge.

returns.desc: a Vertex object if successful

methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
vertex = edge.start

methods.name: used_by?
methods.summary: The used_by? method is used to see if an edge is used by a given Face or Vertex.

params.name: element
params.desc: A Vertex or Face object.

methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0],[100, 100, 0])
# Returns a vertex
vertex = edge.start
# Check to see if the edge is used by the Vertex.
edge.used_by?(vertex)

methods.name: vertices
methods.summary: The vertices method is used to retrieve the vertices on the edge.

returns.desc: an array of Vertex objects

methods.example:
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0])
vertices = edge.vertices

Sketchup::Entities.summary: The Sketchup::Entities class is a collection of Entity objects, either in a Sketchup::ComponentDefinition or directly in the Sketchup::Model. A Sketchup::Entities object corresponds to a drawing context in the GUI.

methods.summary: Instance Methods The #[] method is used to retrieve an entity by its index in an array of entities. The index is a number between 0 and entities.length - 1. In general, it is preferable to use the #each method to iterate though all of the entities in the collection as it will be much more efficient.

methods.name: add_dimension_linear
methods.summary: The #add_dimension_linear method adds a linear dimension to the entities.

params.name: start_pt_or_entity
params.desc: the reference point and/or entity at the start of the dimension. This parameter can take several forms:

params.name: end_pt_or_entity
params.desc: the reference point and/or entity at the end of the dimension. This parameter takes the exact same forms as 'start_pt_or_entity'.

params.name: offset_vector
params.desc: the parallel offset vector from the reference line to the dimension line measured from the 'start' reference point.

params.name: start_instance_path
params.desc: An array containing a Sketchup::InstancePath and a Geom::Point3d.

params.name: end_instance_path
params.desc: An array containing a Sketchup::InstancePath and a Geom::Point3d.

params.name: start_array
params.desc: The Array<Sketchup::Entity> must contain one or more Sketchup::ComponentInstance's and a leaf entity. The leaf entity can be a Sketchup::Vertex, Sketchup::ConstructionPoint, ...

params.name: end_array
params.desc: The Array<Sketchup::Entity> must contain one or more Sketchup::ComponentInstance's and a leaf entity. The leaf entity can be a Sketchup::Vertex, Sketchup::ConstructionPoint, ...

returns.desc: the created dimension

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
# From point to point
dim = entities.add_dimension_linear([0, 0, 0], [50, 0, 0], [0, 20, 0])

# Between edge vertices
edge1 = entities.add_edges([70, 0, 0], [120, 0, 0])[0]
v0 = edge1.start
v1 = edge1.end
dim = entities.add_dimension_linear(v0, v1, [0, 20, 0])

# From an edge's midpoint to a construction point
edge2 = entities.add_edges([150, 0, 0], [200, 0, 0])[0]
p0 = edge2.start.position
p1 = edge2.end.position
mp = Geom::Point3d.new((p0.x + p1.x) / 2.0, (p0.y + p1.y) / 2.0, (p0.z + p1.z) / 2.0)
cp = entities.add_cpoint([150, 40, 0])
dim = entities.add_dimension_linear([edge2, mp], cp, [20, 0, 0])

Added in SketchUp 2019.

methods.name: add_face
methods.summary: The add_face method is used to create a face. You can call this method a number of ways: - entities.add_face(edge1, edge2, edge3, ...) - entities.add_face(edgearray) - entities.add_face(pt1, pt2, pt3, ...) - entities.add_face([pt1, pt2, pt3,...]) - entities.add_face(curve) For the last form that takes a Curve, the curve must be closed - like a circle.

model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities

# Create a group with geometry to transform
group1 = entities.add_group
face1 = group1.entities.add_face([0, 0, 0], [100, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0], [0, 100, 0])
face1.pushpull(-40)

# Raise vertices in selection by their distance to the origin.
with_vertices = group1.entities.select { |entity| entity.respond_to?(:vertices) }
vertices = with_vertices.flat_map(&:vertices).uniq
lengths = vertices.map { |vertex| vertex.position.distance(ORIGIN) }
vectors = lengths.map { |length| Geom::Vector3d.new(0, 0, length) }

entities.transform_by_vectors(vertices, vectors)

methods.name: transform_entities
methods.summary: The transform_entities method is used to apply a transform to several sub-entities all at once. If you are transforming entities in the active drawing context or any of its parent drawing contexts, the transformation will be interpreted as relative to the global coordinate system. Otherwise the transformation will be interpreted as being on the local coordinate system.

params.name: transform
params.desc: The Transformation to apply.

params.name: entities
params.desc: An array or series of entities to transform.

returns.desc: false if the entities array was empty.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities
# Add edges to the model at the origin.
edge1 = entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 100, 100])
edge2 = entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [200, -10, -10])

# After the transformation, the edges will be moved 100 inches
# away from the origin, on the x axis.
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new([100, 0, 0])
entities.transform_entities(transformation, [edge1, edge2])

methods.name: weld
methods.summary: The #weld method takes a set of edges and find all possible chains of edges and connect them with a Sketchup::Curve. A curve will not cross another curve. They will split where multiple curves meet.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
edges = []
edges << entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [100, 20, 0])
edges << entities.add_line([100, 20, 0], [130, 200, 50])
edges << entities.add_line([130, 200, 50], [130, 300, 50])
curves = model.active_entities.weld(edges)
raises: [ArgumentError] if the given entities are not part of the same Sketchup::Entities collection.

Sketchup::EntitiesBuilder.summary: The Sketchup::EntitiesBuilder is an interface to generate bulk geometry with performance in mind. This is particularly useful for importers where the geometry is already well defined and one wants to recreate it without further processing. Before the Entities Builder was introduced there were two ways of adding geometry; the add_* methods of Sketchup::Entities and Geom::PolygonMesh.

methods.name: add_edge
methods.summary: Instance Methods Adds a Sketchup::Edge to the #entities collection.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.entities.build { |builder|
  edge = builder.add_edge([0, 0, 0], [9, 0, 0])
  edge.material = 'red'
}
notes: Does not split intersecting faces or edges.
raises: [ArgumentError] If the points are considered equal.
[RuntimeError] If the builder is not valid.

methods.name: add_edges
methods.summary: Adds a continuous set of Sketchup::Edge's to the #entities collection.

returns.desc: In the array, for each pair in points an edge is returned. If two point are so close they are considered identical then nil is returned.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.entities.build { |builder|
  edges = builder.add_edges([0, 0, 0], [6, 0, 0], [9, 0, 8]) # => 2 edges
  edges.each { |edge|
    edge.material = 'red'
  }
}
notes: Does not split intersecting faces or edges.
raises: [RuntimeError] If the builder is not valid.

methods.name: add_face
methods.summary: Adds a Sketchup::Face to the #entities collection.
methods.example:
Adding a simple face
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.entities.build { |builder|
  face = builder.add_face([[0, 0, 0], [6, 0, 0], [6, 8, 0], [0, 8, 0]])
  face.material = 'red'
}
notes: Does not split intersecting faces or edges.
The inner loops are not validated to be within the bounds of the outer loop.
The inner loops are not validated to be within the bounds of the outer loop.
raises: [ArgumentError] If points are not planar.
[ArgumentError] If any of the loops doesn't have at least 3 points.
[RuntimeError] If the builder is not valid.

methods.name: entities
methods.summary: The Sketchup::Entities collection the Sketchup::EntitiesBuilder will add the geometry to.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.entities.build { |builder|
  p builder.entities == model.entities # => true
}
raises: [RuntimeError] If the builder is not valid.

methods.name: valid?
methods.summary: Indicates whether the builder object is valid and can be used. A builder object is only valid within the scope of the block given to Sketchup::Entities#build. When this return false, calling any other method on the builder will raise an error.
bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2023.0 this returned 0 for success instead of true. In Ruby 0 evaluates as true so conditional logic still worked.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
cached_builder = nil
model.entities.build { |builder|
  p builder.valid? # => true
  cached_builder = builder # Don't hold on to builder objects.
}
p cached_builder.valid? # => false

methods.name: vertex_at
methods.summary: Finds an existing Sketchup::Vertex for the given position, otherwise returns nil.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.entities.build { |builder|
  edge = builder.add_edge([1, 0, 0], [9, 0, 0])
  builder.vertex_at([0, 0, 0]) => nil
  builder.vertex_at([9, 0, 0]) => #<Sketchup::Vertex>
}

If the third parameter, default_value, is not passed and there is no attribute that matches the given name, it returns nil. methods.summary: The #persistent_id method is used to retrieve a unique persistent id assigned to an entity. The persistent id persistent between sessions.

]

methods.name: texture_positioned?
methods.summary: The #texture_positioned? method is used to check if the face has a texture that is positioned. A texture is positioned when it's not using the default texture coordinates. When a user uses the Paint Bucket Tool to apply a material sampled from the Material Browser it will use default texture coordinates and not be positioned. It will be positioned if the user uses the Position Texture Tool.

params.name: front
params.desc: true Checks the front side of the face, false the back side.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities

# Filter the entities to get only the faces

  # Select faces that have manually positioned textures
  # Check both in front face (true) and the back face (false)
  face.texture_positioned?(true) || face.texture_positioned?(false)
}

# 'faces' will contain all faces with manually positioned textures

methods.name: texture_projected?
methods.summary: The #texture_projected? method is used to check if the face has a texture that is projected. A texture is projected when the user enables this property via the Position Texture Tool. It is also projected when the API user passes a projection vector to #position_material.

params.name: front
params.desc: true Checks the front side of the face, false the back side.

methods.name: uv_tile_at
methods.summary: The #uv_tile_at method is used to get the corner positions (model and UV) of a UV tile. The UV tile bounds the given reference point on the plane of the face. If the reference isn't on the plane of the face it will be projected onto it.

params.name: position
params.desc: Model position on the face's plane that will be bounded by the UV tile.

params.name: front
params.desc: true Checks the front side of the face, false the back side.

returns.desc: A set of 8 points. Each stride of two is first a model space point, the second a UV coordinate. nil if the face doesn't have a texture on the given side.

bugs: Fixed in SketchUp 2022.0: If the position argument should line up exact U or V axes of the UV coordinate system the returned set of points won't be correct. A workaround for older SketchUp versions ...
methods.example:
Copy material from front to back
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.active_entities.grep(Sketchup::Face) { |face|
  material = face.material

  if material&.texture.nil?
    face.back_material = material
  end

  reference = face.vertices.first.position
  mapping = face.uv_tile_at(reference, true)
  if face.texture_projected?(true)
    projection = face.get_texture_projection(true)
    face.position_material(material, mapping, false, projection)
  else
    face.position_material(material, mapping, false)
  end
}

methods.name: frameChange
methods.summary: Instance Methods This callback method is called during a slide show or creation of an animation after the camera has been set up, but before the frame is displayed. It gives you a chance to perform your own actions during the animation. The arguments for frameChange method are the scene page that you transition from (from_scene), the scene page that you transition to (to_scene), and a percent_done between 0.0 and ...

params.name: from_scene
params.desc: The previous scene page the view is transitioning from.

params.name: to_scene
params.desc: The selected scene page the view is transitioning towards.

params.name: percent_done
params.desc: The percentage of transition between the two scene pages.

methods.example:
class MyFrameChangeObserver
  def frameChange(from_scene, to_scene, percent_done)
    if percent_done == 0.0

    end
  end
end

methods.summary: The glued_to= method glues this group to a drawing element. When moving this other drawing elment with the Move tool, the glued group moves with it.

model = Sketchup.active_model

Sketchup::Http.summary: The Sketchup::Http module provides interfaces to create asynchronous HTTP requests. This is an alternative to the Net::Http module that comes with Ruby StdLib - which is known to have issues within SketchUp.

Sketchup::Http::Request.summary: Sketchup::Http::Request objects allows you to send HTTP request to HTTP servers.

methods.name: body
methods.summary: Instance Methods Gets the HTTP body that is going to be used when sending the request.

methods.name: body=
methods.summary: Sets the HTTP body that is going to be used when sending the request.

params.name: body
params.desc: A String containing the body.

methods.summary: Cancels the request.

methods.summary: Returns the HTTP headers that are going to be used when sending the request.

methods.summary: Sets the HTTP headers that are going to be used when sending the request.

params.name: headers
params.desc: A key/value pair hash.

methods.name: initialize
methods.summary: The default port is 80, to use a different port define it in the URL when creating a new Sketchup::Http::Request. The #method parameter accepts any custom HTTP method or one of the following: - Sketchup::Http::GET - Sketchup::Http::POST - Sketchup::Http::PUT - Sketchup::Http::DELETE - Sketchup::Http::HEAD - Sketchup::Http::OPTIONS
notes: If no reference is kept to the Sketchup::Http::Request, it can be garbage collected, making the download silently fail. This is especially noticeable for larger downloads that takes longer time.
Do not #cancel the request in the response callback.

methods.name: method
methods.summary: Returns the HTTP method that is going to be used when sending the request.

methods.name: method=
methods.summary: Sets the HTTP method that is going to be used when sending the request. The value can be any custom HTTP method or one of the following: - Sketchup::Http::GET - Sketchup::Http::POST - Sketchup::Http::PUT - Sketchup::Http::DELETE - Sketchup::Http::HEAD - Sketchup::Http::OPTIONS

params.name: method
params.desc: A string containing the HTTP method name.

methods.name: set_download_progress_callback
methods.summary: Adds a download progress callback block that will get called everytime we have received data from the server until the download finishes.
notes: total is -1 if the server doesn't specify a file size in the response header.

methods.name: set_upload_progress_callback
methods.summary: Adds a upload progress callback block that will get called everytime we have uploaded data to the server until the upload finishes.

methods.name: start
methods.summary: Starts the request with optionally a response callback block.
notes: Do not #cancel the request in the response callback.

methods.name: status
methods.summary: Returns the internal status code. It can be one of the following: * Sketchup::Http::STATUS_UNKNOWN * Sketchup::Http::STATUS_SUCCESS * Sketchup::Http::STATUS_PENDING * Sketchup::Http::STATUS_CANCELED * Sketchup::Http::STATUS_FAILED

methods.summary: Returns a copy of the Request's URL.

Sketchup::Http::Response.summary: Sketchup::Http::Response objects allows you to get the response information from the server, you can only receive the Sketchup::Http::Response if you have attached a callback block when calling start from the Sketchup::Http::Request object.

methods.name: body
methods.summary: Instance Methods Gets the HTTP body that was received from the server as a string encoded using the charset provided in the "Content-Type" header of the server response, if no charset is specified, Encoding::ASCII_8BIT will be used.

methods.name: headers
methods.summary: Returns the HTTP headers that were sent by the server.

methods.name: status_code
methods.summary: Returns the HTTP response status code as defined in rfc2616.

Sketchup::Image.summary: An Image object represents a raster image placed in the Model.

methods.name: explode
methods.summary: Instance Methods The explode method is used to explode an image into a face with a texture on it. Note that current versions of SketchUp will return an empty array here. To work around this limitation you can iterate over your entities collection to determine which new entities were created. Versions prior to SketchUp 2015 returned an empty array due to a bug.

returns.desc: entitiesarray - an Array object of entities if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = "Plugins/su_dynamiccomponents/images"
image_file = Sketchup.find_support_file("report_tool.png", path)
image = model.active_entities.add_image(image_file, ORIGIN, 300)
entities = image.explode

methods.name: glued_to
methods.summary: The #glued_to method is used to retrieve the entity that this image is glued to.
methods.example:
point = Geom::Point3d.new(10, 20, 30)
transform = Geom::Transformation.new(point)
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
group = entities.add_group
group.entities.add_face([[0, 0, 0], [10, 0, 0], [10, 10, 0], [0, 10, 0]])
status = group.glued_to

methods.name: glued_to=
methods.summary: The glued_to= method glues this image to a drawing element. When moving this other drawing elment with the Move tool, the image moves with it.

returns.desc: the entity the group was glued to.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities

# Create a face
face = entities.add_face([[0, 0, 0], [100, 0, 0], [100, 100, 0], [0, 100, 0]])

# Create a group
path = "Plugins/su_dynamiccomponents/images"
image_file = Sketchup.find_support_file("report_tool.png", path)
image = model.active_entities.add_image(image_file, ORIGIN, 300)

# Glue the group to the face.
# If you now move the face, the group will follow.
image.glued_to = face
raises: ArgumentError if this would lead to cyclic gluing.

methods.name: height
methods.summary: The height method is used to retrieve the height of the image. The height is given in inches.

returns.desc: height - the height of the model if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
height = image.height

methods.name: height=
methods.summary: The height= method is used to set the height of the image. The height is set in inches.

params.name: height
params.desc: The height, in inches, to set the image.

returns.desc: height - the new height if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
UI.messagebox "Before adjustment"
height = image.height = 400

methods.name: image_rep
methods.summary: The #image_rep method returns a copy of a Sketchup::ImageRep object representing the pixel data.
bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2021.1, SketchUp crashes when the Image is corrupt and lacks image data.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = "Plugins/su_dynamiccomponents/images"
image_file = Sketchup.find_support_file("report_tool.png", path)
image = model.active_entities.add_image(image_file, ORIGIN, 300)
image_rep = image.image_rep
raises: ArgumentError if the Image is corrupt and lacks image data.

methods.name: normal
methods.summary: The normal method is used to retrieve the 3D Vector that is perpendicular to the plane of the image.

returns.desc: vector - a Vector3d object if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
vector = image.normal

methods.name: origin
methods.summary: The origin method is used to retrieve the 3D point that defines the origin of the image.

returns.desc: point - a Point3d object containing the origin location if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
origin = image.origin
puts origin.inspect

methods.name: origin=
methods.summary: The #origin= method is used to set the 3D point as the origin of the image.

params.name: point
params.desc: A Point3d object with the new origin.

returns.desc: point - the Point3d object representing the newly established origin if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
pt2 = Geom::Point3d.new 100,100,100
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
UI.messagebox "Before Move"
origin = image.origin=pt2
puts origin.inspect

methods.name: path
methods.summary: The path method is used to retrieve the path of the file defining the image.

returns.desc: path - the path for the image file if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
path = image.path

methods.name: pixelheight
methods.summary: The pixelheight method is used to retrieve the height of the image file in pixels.

returns.desc: height - the height of the image in pixels if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
pixelheight = image.pixelheight

methods.name: pixelwidth
methods.summary: The pixelwidth method is used to retrieve the width of the image file in pixels.

returns.desc: width - the width of the image in pixels if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
pixelwidth = image.pixelwidth

methods.name: size=
methods.summary: The size= method is used to set the width and height of the image, in inches.

params.name: width
params.desc: The width of the image.

params.name: height
params.desc: The height of the image.

returns.desc: size - the new width and height of the image if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
UI.messagebox "Before Resize"
size = image.size= 500,500

methods.name: transform!
methods.summary: The transform! method is used to apply a transformation to the image.

params.name: transform
params.desc: A Transformation object.

returns.desc: image - the transformed Image object if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
point = Geom::Point3d.new 100,100,100
t = Geom::Transformation.new point
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
UI.messagebox "Before Move"
image = image.transform! t

methods.name: transformation
methods.summary: The transformation method is used to retrieve the transformation for the image.

returns.desc: transformation - a Transformation object if successful

methods.example:
# Add an image to the model.
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
path = Sketchup.find_support_file('report_tool.png', 'Plugins/su_dynamiccomponents/images')
point = Geom::Point3d.new(100,100,100)
image = entities.add_image(path, point, 300)

trans = image.transformation

methods.name: transformation=
methods.summary: The transformation= method is used to set the transformation for the image.

params.name: transform
params.desc: The Transformation object to apply

returns.desc: image - the newly transformed image

methods.example:
# Add an image to the model.
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
path = Sketchup.find_support_file('report_tool.png', 'Plugins/su_dynamiccomponents/images')
point = Geom::Point3d.new(100,100,100)
image = entities.add_image(path, point, 300)

new_transform = Geom::Transformation.new([100,0,0])
image.transformation = new_transform

methods.name: width
methods.summary: The width method is used to retrieve the width of the image. The width is given in inches.

returns.desc: width - the width of the image if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png",
  "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
width = image.width

methods.name: width=
methods.summary: The width= method is used to set the width of the image. The width is set in inches.

params.name: width
params.desc: The width, in inches, to set the image.

returns.desc: width - the new width if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
UI.messagebox "Before adjustment"
width = image.width=400

methods.name: zrotation
methods.summary: The zrotation method is used to get the angle that the image is rotated about the normal vector from an arbitrary X axis.

returns.desc: vector - a Vector3d object if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
path = Sketchup.find_support_file "report_tool.png", "Tools/DynamicComponents/images"
pt = Geom::Point3d.new
entities = model.active_entities
image = entities.add_image path, pt, 300
zrotation = image.zrotation

methods.name: bits_per_pixel
methods.summary: Instance Methods The #bits_per_pixel method gets the number of bits per pixel in the image.
methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image.jpg")
bpp = image_rep.bits_per_pixel

methods.name: color_at_uv
methods.summary: The #color_at_uv method returns a color corresponding to the UV texture coordinates. 0.0, 0.0 maps to the bottom left and 1.0, 1.0 to the top right of the image.

params.name: u
params.desc: The U texture coordinate.

params.name: v
params.desc: The V texture coordinate.

params.name: bilinear
params.desc: Use bilinear texture filtering. This interpolates the colors instead of picking the nearest neighbor.

methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image.jpg")
color = image_rep.color_at_uv(0.7, 0.5, false)

methods.name: colors
methods.summary: The #colors method returns an array of Sketchup::Color for each pixel in the image.
methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image.jpg")
colors = image_rep.colors

methods.name: data
methods.summary: The #data method gets the pixel data for an image in a string of bytes.
methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image.jpg")
byte_string = image_rep.data
byte_string.each_byte { |byte| puts byte, ' ' }
notes: The byte order of the pixels are RGB(A) on macOS and BGR(A) on Windows.

methods.name: height
methods.summary: The #height method returns the height of an image.
methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image.jpg")
image_rep.height

methods.name: initialize
methods.summary: The #initialize method creates a new image object. The image object will have no data if a path to the image is not provided.
methods.example:
Default constructor
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
# Use #set_data or #load_file to add image data.
raises: [ArgumentError] if the file path or image is invalid.

methods.name: load_file
methods.summary: The #load_file method loads image data from the specified file.
methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image.jpg")
raises: [ArgumentError] if the filepath or image is invalid.

methods.name: row_padding
methods.summary: The #row_padding method returns the size of the row padding of an image in bytes.
methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image.jpg")
image_rep.row_padding

methods.name: save_file
methods.summary: The #save_file method saves an image data object to an image file specified by a path.
methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image1.jpg")
# do stuff with the image representation
image_rep.save_file("/path/to/save/image2.jpg")

methods.name: set_data
methods.summary: The #set_data method discards any existing data and sets new pixel data for the Sketchup::ImageRep.

params.name: width
params.desc: The width of the pixel data. Must be greater than 0.

params.name: height
params.desc: The height of the pixel data. Must be greater than 0.

params.name: bits_per_pixel
params.desc: The bits per pixel for the pixel data. Must be either 8/24/32.

params.name: row_padding
params.desc: The row padding for the pixel data which is sized in bytes. Row padding is used to pad each row with zeros so that each scanline on the pixel data will end on the data-type boundary.

params.name: pixel_data
params.desc: The binary string containing the pixel data representing the new image.

methods.example:
Setting new data
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
width = 800
height = 600
bpp = 24
pixel = [127, 127, 127].pack("C*")
pixels = pixel * width * height
image_rep.set_data(width, height, bpp, 0, pixels)
image_rep.save_file(UI.savepanel)
notes: The byte order of the pixels are RGB(A) on macOS and BGR(A) on Windows.
The encoding of the pixel_data String parameter should be ASCII-8BIT. Any other encoding could corrupt the binary data. Using Array#pack("C*") gives correct encoding.
raises: [ArgumentError] If width, height, bits_per_pixel or pixel_data are invalid.
[TypeError] If width, height, bits_per_pixel or pixel_data are wrong data types.

methods.name: size
methods.summary: The #size method gets the total size of the image data in bytes.
methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image.jpg")
data_size = image_rep.size

methods.name: width
methods.summary: The #width method returns the width of an image.
methods.example:
image_rep = Sketchup::ImageRep.new
image_rep.load_file("/path/to/image.jpg")
image_rep.width

Sketchup::Importer.summary: The Importer interface lets you build your own importers for SketchUp. To use this, you create a subclass of Importer and implement all of the methods described below. This will make your importer appear in the list that users see under File > Import, and you can use Ruby to do all of the work of opening the file and creating whatever you need inside SketchUp.

methods.name: description
methods.summary: Instance Methods This method is called by SketchUp to determine the description that appears in the File > Import dialog's pulldown list of valid importers. Though it is common for the description to include the file extension supported by the importer (such as "Text Importer (.txt)"), the actual extension is defined in the file_extension method.

returns.desc: description - a brief string description

methods.example:
def description
  return "Custom Text Importer (*.txt)"
end

methods.name: do_options
methods.summary: This method is called by SketchUp when the user clicks on the "Options" button inside the File > Import dialog. You can use it to gather and store settings for your importer. Only applicable if the importer supports options, meaning its supports_options method returns true.

returns.desc: id - an id string

methods.example:
def id
  return "com.sketchup.importers.custom_txt"
end

methods.name: file_extension
methods.summary: This method is called by SketchUp to determine a single file extension is associated with your importer. Only files that match this extension will be shown to the user as they browse their harddrive for things to import. Ruby importers are only allowed to support a single extension.

returns.desc: extension - typically a 3-letter string

methods.example:
def file_extension
  return "txt"
end

methods.name: id
methods.summary: This method is called by SketchUp to determine a unique identifier for your importer, typically something like "com.sketchup.importers.dxf".

returns.desc: id - an id string

methods.example:
def id
  return "com.sketchup.importers.custom_txt"
end

methods.name: load_file
methods.summary: This method is called by SketchUp after the user has selected a file to import. This is where you do the real work by opening the file via Ruby's File object and processing it in whatever way you need. You must return an integer success code to SketchUp when you are done. These are the codes that SketchUp understands:

params.name: file_path
params.desc: Absolute path to the file the user selected

params.name: status
params.desc: The status of the import so far. Contains true.

returns.desc: success - an integer status code. See above.

methods.example:
def load_file(file_path, status)
  # Here is where you would open the file and process it.
  puts file_path

  return Sketchup::Importer::ImportSuccess
end

methods.name: supports_options?
methods.summary: This method is called by SketchUp to determine if the "Options" button inside the File > Import dialog should be enabled while your importer is selected.

returns.desc: supports_options - a boolean

methods.example:
def supports_options?
  return true
end

Sketchup::InputPoint.summary: The Sketchup::InputPoint class is used to pick 3d points and/or entities that reside under the current cursor location, similar to native Line tool and other drawing tools. Unlike Sketchup::PickHelper, Sketchup::InputPoint uses inference, i.e. "snaps" to vertices and other entities when the cursor is close to them.

methods.summary: Instance Methods The == method is used to determine if two input points are the same.

params.name: inputpoint2
params.desc: The second input point in the comparison.

returns.desc: status - true if the InputPoint objects are the same object. False if the objects are not the same.

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = Sketchup::InputPoint.new
ip2 = view.inputpoint x,y
# Copy the contents of inputpoint2 into inputpoint1
ip1.copy! ip2
# Returns true
status = ip1 == ip2

methods.name: clear
methods.summary: The clear method is used to clear the input point. This sets it to an empty state. After calling this, valid? will return false.

returns.desc: inputpoint - the cleared (empty) input point if this successful

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
# Returns true
ip = ip1.clear

methods.name: copy!
methods.summary: The copy! method is used to copy the data from a second input point into this input point.

params.name: inputpoint
params.desc: The second input point.

returns.desc: inputpoint - the new input point that received the copy if successful

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = Sketchup::InputPoint.new
ip2 = view.inputpoint x,y
# Copy the contents of inputpoint2 into inputpoint1
ip = ip1.copy! ip2

methods.name: degrees_of_freedom
methods.summary: The degrees_of_freedom method retrieves the number of degrees of freedom there are for an input point. If you are just getting a point in space, then the degrees_of_freedom will be 3 - meaning that there is nothing about the point that would constrain its position. If you are on a face, then the degrees_of_freedom will be 2 meaning that you can only move on the plane of the face.

returns.desc: degrees_of_freedom - see comments.

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
dof = ip1.degrees_of_freedom

methods.name: depth
methods.summary: The depth method retrieves the depth of an inference if it is coming from a component. If the InputPoint is not getting a position from inside a component, this method will return 0. Otherwise it returns the depth of the entity in a nested component that is providing the position.

returns.desc: depth - a number representing the depth of the inputpoint (inside groups and components) if successful

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
d = ip1.depth

methods.name: display?
methods.summary: The display? method is used to determine if the input point has anything to draw. If the method returns true, then the draw method will draw something.

returns.desc: status - true if the draw method will draw something, false if the draw method has nothing to draw

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
status = ip1.display

methods.name: draw
methods.summary: The draw method is used to draw the input point. This is useful for showing an InputPoint from within the draw method of a tool that you have implemented in Ruby. Additional examples are available in the Plugins/examples directory.

params.name: view
params.desc: The current view.

returns.desc: view

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
ip = ip1.draw view

methods.name: edge
methods.summary: The edge method is used to retrieve the edge if the input point is getting its position from a point on an Edge.

returns.desc: edge - an Edge object if successful, or nil if unsuccessful

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
e = ip1.edge

methods.name: face
methods.summary: The face method retrieves the face at or behind the input point. This can be used to determine a plane, similar to what native Rotate tool does.
methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
f = ip1.face
notes: The InputPoint doesn't necessarily lie on the face, but can be e.g. on an edge in front of the face.

methods.name: initialize
methods.summary: The new method is used to create a new InputPoint object.

params.name: pt_or_vertex
params.desc: An optional Point3d or Vertex where the new InputPoint should be created.

methods.example:
ip1 = Sketchup::InputPoint.new

# Or you can construct it at an arbitrary location.
starting_point = Geom::Point3d.new(100, 200, 300)
ip2 = Sketchup::InputPoint.new(starting_point)
notes: Prior to SketchUp 2019 it was not possible to sub-class Sketchup::InputPoint due to a bug in how SketchUp initialized the class.

methods.name: instance_path
methods.summary: The #instance_path method retrieves the instance path for the picked point. The returned instance_path is a copy of what the input point is holding on to at the moment you access it. Your copy will not update if you make new picks with the input point. If there has been no valid pick it will return `nil`.
methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip = view.inputpoint(x, y)
instance_path = ip.instance_path

methods.name: pick
methods.summary: The #pick method is used to get a input point at a specific screen position.

params.name: x
params.desc: Screen coordinate in physical pixels.

params.name: y
params.desc: Screen coordinate in physical pixels.

params.name: inputpoint
params.desc: A second input point used as a reference for the pick.

returns.desc: true if a valid input point was picked and it is different than it was before.

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100 # Screen coordinate
y = 200 # Screen coordinate
inputpoint = view.inputpoint(x, y)
inputpoint2 = Sketchup::InputPoint.new(Geom::Point3d.new(100, 250, 300))
inputpoint.pick(view, x, y)
inputpoint.pick(view, x, y, inputpoint2)
notes: Signature for versions prior to SketchUp 2025.0
Signature for versions prior to SketchUp 2025.0

methods.name: position
methods.summary: The position method is used to get the 3D point from the input point.

returns.desc: point - a Point3d object position for the input point if successful

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
point = ip1.position

methods.name: tooltip
methods.summary: The tooltip method is used to retrieve the string that is the tool tip to display for the input point.

returns.desc: tip - a string tooltip or an empty string (if the input point doesn't provide a tooltip).

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
# Click on a face and you get "On Face"
tip = ip1.tooltip

methods.name: transformation
methods.summary: The transformation method retrieves the Transformation object for the input point. If the InputPoint object is getting its position from something inside of a component instance, this method returns the Transformation of the component instance. Otherwise it returns the identity Transformation.

returns.desc: transformation - the Transformation for the input point if successful

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
# In this case, returning the identity transformation
tform = ip1.transformation

methods.name: valid?
methods.summary: The valid? method is used to determine if an input point has valid data. You must have called the pick method to set the data before it is valid.

returns.desc: status - true if the input point has valid data, false if it does not have valid data.

methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
x = 100
y = 100
ip1 = view.inputpoint x,y
status = ip1.valid?

methods.name: vertex

Sketchup::InstancePath.summary: The Sketchup::InstancePath class represent the instance path to a given entity within the model hierarchy.

methods.summary: Instance Methods

methods.summary: The elements of an instance path can be accessed similarly to an array.

model = Sketchup.active_model

  # do something

Sketchup::Layer.summary: The Layer class contains methods modifying and extracting information for a layer.

methods.summary: Instance Methods The #<=> method is used to compare two layers based on their names. This enables the Ruby Array#sort method to sort SketchUp layers.

returns.desc: -1 if layer1 is less than layer2. 1 if layer2 is less than layer1. 0 if layer1 and layer2 are equal.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
layers = model.layers

layer1 = layers[0]
layer2 = layers[1]
status = layer1 <=> layer2

methods.summary: The #== method is used to determine if two layers are the same.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
layers = model.layers
layer1 = layers.add("Test layer 1")
layer2 = layers.add("Test layer 2")
equal = layer1 == layer2

methods.name: color
methods.summary: The #color method is used to retrieve the color of the layer.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
layers = model.layers
new_layer = layers.add('Test layer')

methods.name: color=

model = Sketchup.active_model

layers = model.layers
new_layer = layers.add ("test layer")
name = new_layer.display_name

methods.name: folder
methods.summary: The #folder method is used to return the parent layer folder of a layer.

returns.desc: nil if the folder is a direct child to the layer manager.

methods.name: name=

methods.name: page_behavior
methods.summary: The #page_behavior method is used to retrieve the visibility behavior of the layer for new pages and existing pages. For example, you may want your layer to be visible or hidden by default in any new pages (aka Scenes) created by the user. A page keeps a list of layers that do not have their default behavior. If a layer is not in that list, then it is set to its default visibility determined by one of these values:

returns.desc: an integer representing the current behavior of the layer.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
layers = model.layers
layer = layers.add('Test Layer')
hidden_by_default = (layer.page_behavior & LAYER_HIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT) ==
                    LAYER_HIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT

methods.name: page_behavior=
methods.summary: The #page_behavior= method is used to control the layer's visibility behavior on existing and new pages. When you Update a page (as opposed to creating a new page) the current visibility of the layer is used. The behavior is composed of a combination of these flags:
bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2014 the LAYER_HIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT flag would trigger the validation check in SketchUp that would reset the #page_behavior of the layer.
methods.example:

layer = layers.add('Test Layer')

methods.name: remove
methods.summary: Remove the given layer from the model, optionally removing the geometry.

params.name: remove_geometry
params.desc: If true, geometry in the removed layer will be removed as well. If false (which is the default), this geometry will be placed on Layer 0.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
# Remove layer by layer reference.
layer = Sketchup.active_model.layers.add("MyLayer")
Sketchup.active_model.layers.remove(layer)

# Remove layer by name.
Sketchup.active_model.layers.add("MyLayer")
Sketchup.active_model.layers.remove("MyLayer")

# Remove layer by index.
Sketchup.active_model.layers.remove(1)

# Remove layer and the entities on the layer.
edge = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [9, 9, 9])
edge.layer = Sketchup.active_model.layers.add("MyLayer")
Sketchup.active_model.layers.remove("MyLayer", true)

Sketchup::Licensing.summary: The Sketchup::Licensing module contains methods for extensions purchased from Extension Warehouse to check their licensing status. It is advised to place these calls inside encrypted Ruby (.rbe) files. This API is also exposed via the SketchUp C API. Extensions that already use native code should prefer using the native API, which should be more secure than their Ruby API counterparts.

methods.name: get_extension_license
methods.summary: Class Methods Gets a license for a given extension.

params.name: extension_id
params.desc: The Extension Warehouse UUID for the desired extension.

returns.desc: An object representing licensing state for the extension. Do not store this object; retrieve it again when needed since licensing state may have changed.

methods.example:
ext_id = "4e215280-dd23-40c4-babb-b8a8dd29d5ee"
ext_lic = Sketchup::Licensing.get_extension_license(ext_id)
if ext_lic.licensed?
   puts "Extension is licensed."
end

Sketchup::Licensing::ExtensionLicense.summary: The Sketchup::Licensing::ExtensionLicense class is used to store extension license information. An instance of this class is returned by Sketchup::Licensing.get_extension_license. Note that this is a temporary object representing the extension licensing state for the moment it was returned. It will not reflect any licensing state changes that may occur.

methods.name: days_remaining
methods.summary: Instance Methods The days_remaining method is used to get the number of days remaining until license expiration.

returns.desc: Integer - Number of days until license expiration. Zero if a permanent license or not licensed.

methods.example:
ext_id = "4e215280-dd23-40c4-babb-b8a8dd29d5ee"
ext_lic = Sketchup::Licensing.get_extension_license(ext_id)
if ext_lic.days_remaining != 0
   puts "The license will expire in #{ext_lic.days_remaining} days."
end

methods.name: error_description
methods.summary: The error_description method is used to obtain error information in case of failure to acquire a license. This is meant to aid in debugging only. Extensions should not rely on any exact error description.

returns.desc: String - error description.

methods.example:
ext_id = "4e215280-dd23-40c4-babb-b8a8dd29d5ee"
ext_lic = Sketchup::Licensing.get_extension_license(ext_id)
if !ext_lic.licensed?
   puts ext_lic.error_description
end

methods.name: licensed?
methods.summary: The licensed? method is used to decide whether the extension is licensed to run or not.

returns.desc: Boolean - true if the extension is allowed to run, false if it is not licensed and should quit.

methods.example:
ext_id = "4e215280-dd23-40c4-babb-b8a8dd29d5ee"
ext_lic = Sketchup::Licensing.get_extension_license(ext_id)
if ext_lic.licensed?
   puts "Extension is licensed."
end

methods.name: state
methods.summary: The state method returns a constant indicating the specific licensing state. These should be used for informational purposes only and not to decide if the extension is licensed to run. For that, please use the licensed? method.

returns.desc: Integer - One of Sketchup::Licensing::LICENSED, Sketchup::Licensing::EXPIRED, Sketchup::Licensing::TRIAL, Sketchup::Licensing::TRIAL_EXPIRED, Sketchup::Licensing::NOT_LICENSED

methods.example:
ext_id = "4e215280-dd23-40c4-babb-b8a8dd29d5ee"
ext_lic = Sketchup::Licensing.get_extension_license(ext_id)
if ext_lic.state == Sketchup::Licensing::TRIAL_EXPIRED
   puts "Trial period has expired."
end

Sketchup::LoadHandler.summary: The main purpose of the LoadHandler interface is to be used as an optional second parameter of the Sketchup::DefinitionList#load_from_url method. Its methods that require implementation handle the process of downloading and managing the state of the load operation, including progress updates and error handling.

methods.name: cancelled?
methods.summary: Instance Methods This method is called when the download is canceled by the user.
methods.example:
def cancelled?
  # You could, for example, show a messagebox after X seconds asking if the
  # user wants to cancel the download. If this method returns true, then
  # the download cancels.
  return false
end

methods.name: onFailure
methods.summary: This method is called when the download unsuccessfully completes
methods.example:
def onFailure(message)
  self.error = message
  Sketchup::set_status_text('')
end

methods.name: onPercentChange
methods.summary: This method is triggered whenever the percent value updates.

methods.name: onSuccess
methods.summary: This method is called when the download successfully completes
methods.example:
def onSuccess
  Sketchup::set_status_text('')
end

Sketchup::Loop.summary: Loop is a low level topology class that will not need to be used often. A Loop is a chain of Edges that bound a Face.

methods.name: convex?
methods.summary: Instance Methods Determine if the loop is convex.

returns.desc: status - true if convex, false if not convex.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.active_entities
points = []
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 200, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 200, 0)
face = entities.add_face(points)
loop = face.outer_loop
if loop.convex?
  puts "Loop is convex."
else
  puts "Loop is not convex."
end

methods.name: edges
methods.summary: Get an array of the edges that define the loop in an ordered sequence.

returns.desc: edges - an array of Edge objects if successful.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.active_entities
points = []
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 200, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 200, 0)
face = entities.add_face(points)
loop = face.outer_loop
edges = loop.edges

methods.name: edgeuses
methods.summary: Get an array of the EdgeUse objects that define this loop in an ordered sequence.

returns.desc: edgeuses - an array of EdgeUse objects if successful.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.active_entities
points = []
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 200, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 200, 0)
face = entities.add_face(points)
loop = face.outer_loop
edgeuses = loop.edgeuses

methods.name: face
methods.summary: Get the Face object that is bounded by this loop.

returns.desc: face - a Face object if successful

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.active_entities
points = []
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 200, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 200, 0)
face = entities.add_face(points)
loop = face.outer_loop
loop_face = loop.face

methods.name: outer?
methods.summary: Determine if this is an outer loop. Each face has one outer loop, and will have one loop for each hole.

returns.desc: status - true if the loop is an outer loop, false if it is not an outer loop.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.active_entities
points = []
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 200, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 200, 0)
face = entities.add_face(points)
loop = face.outer_loop
if loop.outer?
  puts "Loop is an outer loop."
else
  puts "Loop is not an outer loop."
end

methods.name: vertices
methods.summary: Get an array of the vertices that define the loop in an ordered sequence.

returns.desc: vertices - an array of Vertex objects if successful.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.active_entities
points = []
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 0, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(100, 200, 0)
points << Geom::Point3d.new(0, 200, 0)
face = entities.add_face(points)
loop = face.outer_loop
vertices = loop.vertices

Sketchup::Material.summary: The Sketchup::Material class represents a Sketchup::Texture or Sketchup::Color that can be applied to Sketchup::Drawingelements. It is most often applied to Sketchup::Faces. You can pass any object that can be used as a material to a method that requires a material. Objects include actual Sketchup::Material, Sketchup::Color, and classes that can be converted to a color.

methods.summary: Instance Methods The #<=> method is used to compare two materials based on #display_name.

returns.desc: 0 if they are equal, 1 if material1 > material2, -1 if material1 < material2

methods.example:
materials =  Sketchup.active_model.materials
m1 = materials.add('Joe')
m2 = materials.add('Fred')
m1 <=> m2
# > 1

methods.summary: The #== method is used to test if two materials are the same.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
materials = model.materials
m1 = materials.add('Joe')
m2 = materials.add('Fred')
m1 == m2
# > false

methods.name: alpha
methods.summary: The #alpha method is used to get the opacity of the material. The value will be between 0.0 and 1.0. A value of 0.0 means that the material is completely transparent. A value of 1.0 means that the material is completely opaque.

returns.desc: A value between 0.0 and 1.0.

methods.example:
material = Sketchup.active_model.materials.add('Example')
material.alpha
# > 1.0

methods.name: alpha=
methods.summary: The #alpha= method is used to set the opacity of the material. The value must be between 0.0 and 1.0. A value of 0.0 means that the material is completely transparent. A value of 1.0 means that the material is completely opaque.

params.name: alpha
params.desc: An alpha value between 0.0 and 1.0.

methods.example:
material =  Sketchup.active_model.materials.add('Example')
material.alpha = 0.5

methods.name: ao_enabled=
methods.example:
material = Sketchup.active_model.materials.add("Material")
material.ao_enabled = true
raises: [ArgumentError] if the ambient occlusion texture is not set before enabling ambient occlusion.

methods.name: ao_enabled?
methods.example:
material = Sketchup.active_model.materials.add("Material")
material.ao_enabled?
# > false
notes: There is no setter for this property. Instead it's dictated whether a #ao_texture is set.

methods.name: ao_strength

returns.desc: A value between 0.0 and 1.0.

methods.example:

material.ao_texture = 'path/to/ao_texture.png'
material.ao_strength
# > 1.0

params.name: strenght

methods.name: color
methods.summary: The #color method is used to retrieve the color of the material. If it uses a colorized Sketchup::Texture, this will return the average color of the texture.
methods.example:
materials = Sketchup.active_model.materials.add('Example')
material.color = 'red'
color = material.color
notes: The alpha value of the Sketchup::Color object is not used for the material's transparency. This is controlled by the #alpha property in order for textured materials to also have transparency.

methods.name: color=
methods.summary: The #color= method is used to set the color of the material. If the material has a Sketchup::Texture, then this turns it into a colorized texture. To reset the color of a material with a colorized texture, set the color to nil. If the texture is not colorized it'll be reset to some undefined default color.

params.name: color
params.types: Sketchup::Color, String, Array(Numeric, Numeric, Numeric, Numeric), Integer, nil
params.desc: Any value you can create a Sketchup::Color from or nil.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
materials = model.materials
material = materials.add('Joe')
material.color = 'red'
notes: The alpha value of the Sketchup::Color object is not used for the material's transparency. This is controlled by the #alpha property in order for textured materials to also have transparency.

methods.name: colorize_deltas
methods.summary: The #colorize_deltas method retrieves the HLS delta for colorized materials.

returns.desc: An array of floats representing the HLS delta.

methods.example:
material = Sketchup.active_model.materials.add('Example')
h, l, s = material.colorize_deltas

methods.name: colorize_type
methods.summary: The #colorize_type method retrieves the type of colorization of the material. Colorize Types[#normal_style_summary]: - Sketchup::Material::COLORIZE_SHIFT - Sketchup::Material::COLORIZE_TINT

returns.desc: One of Sketchup::Material::COLORIZE_* values.

methods.example:
material = Sketchup.active_model.materials.add('Example')
type = material.colorize_type
notes: This value is only relevant when the #materialType is set to Sketchup::Material::MATERIAL_COLORIZED_TEXTURED.

methods.name: colorize_type=
methods.summary: The #colorize_type= method set the type of colorization of the material. Colorize Types[#normal_style_summary]: - Sketchup::Material::COLORIZE_SHIFT - Sketchup::Material::COLORIZE_TINT

params.name: type
params.desc: One of Sketchup::Material::COLORIZE_* values.

methods.example:
material = Sketchup.active_model.materials.add('Example')

notes: This value is only relevant when the #materialType is set to Sketchup::Material::MATERIAL_COLORIZED_TEXTURED.

methods.name: display_name
methods.summary: The #display_name method retrieves the name that is displayed within SketchUp for the material. This should be used when presenting the name in the UI, but the returned name cannot be used as a key in Sketchup::Model#materials.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
materials = model.materials
material = materials.add('[Joe]')
# Use .name for the internal name of a material
puts material.name # Outputs "[Joe]"
# Use .display_name for presenting the material name
# to the UI like SketchUp does.
puts material.display_name # Outputs "Joe"

methods.name: materialType
methods.summary: The #materialType method retrieves the type of the material. Types[#material_type_constant_summary]: - 0 = solid (Sketchup::Material::MATERIAL_SOLID) - 1 = textured (Sketchup::Material::MATERIAL_TEXTURED) - 2 = colorized textured (Sketchup::Material::MATERIAL_COLORIZED_TEXTURED) The constants were added in SketchUp 2015.

returns.desc: One of Sketchup::Material::MATERIAL_* values.

methods.example:
material = Sketchup.active_model.materials.add('Example')
material.materialType == Sketchup::Material::MATERIAL_SOLID
# > true

bugs: On SketchUp versions prior to 2014 there is a bug in this method that could potentially lead to file corruption. If you call #remove on a material that is painted onto any entity in the active model ...
methods.example:
Logic for removing a given material of an entity:
# @param [Sketchup::Entity] entity
# @param [Sketchup::Material] material_to_remove
def remove_material(entity, material_to_remove)
  if entity.respond_to?(:material) do
    if entity.material.equal?(material_to_remove) do
      entity.material = nil
    end
  end
  # for entities that have a back material
  if entity.respond_to?(:back_material) do
    if entity.back_material.equal?(material_to_remove) do
      entity.back_material = nil
    end
  end
end
