methods.example:
Traversing every visible entity in the model
module Example

  def self.instance?(entity)
    entity.is_a?(Sketchup::ComponentInstance) || entity.is_a?(Sketchup::Group)
  end

  # Walk the visible entities in the model, taking into account
  # "DrawHiddenGeometry" and "DrawHiddenObjects" rendering options.
  def self.walk(entities, transformation = IDENTITY, path = [], &block)
    entities.each { |entity|
      entity_path = path + [entity]
      next unless entity.model.drawing_element_visible?(entity_path)
      block.call(entity, transformation, path)
      if instance?(entity)
        child_entities = entity.definition.entities
# ...
raises: [ArgumentError] if the instance_path is not valid.

For SketchUp Pro 7.1+, valid extensions include dae, kmz, 3ds, dwg, dxf, fbx, obj, wrl, and xsi. SketchUp Free only supports dae and kmz.

bugs: IFC export on ARM macs isn't working for SketchUp 2022-2025.
methods.example:
General use
model = Sketchup.active_model
show_summary = true

# Export dwg file on a PC, showing a summary when complete.
status = model.export('c:\my_export.dwg', show_summary)

# Export kmz file on Mac (note the absolute file path), without summary.
status = model.export('/Library/my_export.kmz')

# Export pdf file on a PC, showing a summary when complete.
options_hash = { :show_summary => true,
                 :output_profile_lines => false,
                 :map_fonts => false,
                 :model_units => Length::Meter }
status = model.export('c:/my_export.pdf', options_hash)

# Or for a COLLADA (.dae) file.
options_hash = { :triangulated_faces => true,
# ...
raises: [ArgumentError] If the file extension is unsupported.

methods.name: find_entity_by_id
methods.summary: Finds and returns entities by their entityID or GUID. GUIDs looked up are only relevant to Group and ComponentInstance as these GUIDs are persistent. ComponentDefinition and Model GUIDs are not persistent and are not looked up.

params.name: ids_or_array
params.desc: Pass either a series of ids or a single array containing ids. Ids must either be entityID Integers or GUID Strings.

returns.desc: Returns an array with Entity objects for each id found and nil otherwise. Single Entity or nil when called with a single id.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model

# Look up by entityID.
entity_id = model.entities.add_line([0,0,0], [9,9,9]).entityID
entity = model.find_entity_by_id(entity_id)

# Look up by GUID.

methods.name: raytest
methods.summary: The #raytest method is used to cast a ray (line) through the model and return the first thing that the ray hits. A ray is a two element array containing a point and a vector [Geom::Point3d, Geom::Vector3d]. The point defines the start point of the ray and the vector defines the direction. If direction can not be normalized (e.g. direction = [0, 0, 0]), direction is taken as a point the ray intersects.

params.name: ray
params.desc: A two element array containing a point and a vector.

params.name: wysiwyg_flag
params.desc: An optional boolean, added in SU8 M1, indicating whether or not to consider hidden geometry in intersect computations. If this flag is not specified, it defaults to true (WYSIWYG) - i.e. hidden ...

returns.desc: The first value is a Geom::Point3d where the item that the ray passed through exists. The second element is the instance path array of the entity that the ray hit. For example, if the ray hits a face that is contained by a component instance the instance path would be [Component1]. If the ray hit a face that is contained by a component instance, which is contained by another component instance and so on, the instance path would be [Component1, Component2, Component3...].

methods.example:
Using a pickray from the view
model = Sketchup.active_model
ray = model.active_view.pickray(200, 400) # Screen coordinates
item = model.raytest(ray)

methods.name: start_operation
signatures: start_operation(op_name, disable_ui = false, next_transparent = false, transparent = false)
methods.summary: The #start_operation method is used to notify SketchUp that a new operation (which can be undone) is starting. The op_name argument is a description for the operation that is displayed adjacent to the Edit > Undo menu item. Make sure to provide a user friendly name for your operation.

params.name: op_name
params.desc: name of the operation visible in the UI

params.name: disable_ui
params.desc: if set to true, then SketchUp's tendency to update the user interface after each geometry change will be suppressed. This can result in much faster Ruby code execution if the operation involves ...

params.name: next_transparent
params.desc: Deprecated! if set to true, then whatever operation comes after this one will be appended into one combined operation, allowing the user the undo both actions with a single undo command. This ...

params.name: transparent
params.desc: if set to true, then this operation will append to the previous operation. This is particularly useful for creating observers that react to user actions without littering the undo stack with extra ...

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful

methods.example:
Observer Operation since SU2016
class MyDefinitionsObserver < Sketchup::DefinitionObserver
  def onComponentAdded(definitions, definition)
    return if definition.deleted?
    # The operation name won't be displayed when the fourth argument is
    # +true+. It will absorb into the previous operation.
    definition.model.start_operation('Tag It', true, false, true)
    definition.set_attribute('MyExtension', 'Tag', 'You are it')
    definition.model.commit_operation
  end
end

observer = MyDefinitionsObserver.new
model = Sketchup.active_model
model.definitions.add_observer(observer)
notes: Operations in SketchUp are sequential and cannot be nested. If you start a new Ruby operation while another is still open, you will implicitly close the first one.
raises: [RuntimeError] if called within the context of Sketchup::Entities#build.

Sketchup::Overlay.summary: An Overlay provides contextual model information directly in the viewport. This can be presented in 2D and 3D. Examples can be annotations or analytical model information such as geometry analysis, energy analysis, etc. The overlay feature is not intended as a mechanism to provide custom entities to SketchUp. Whatever overlays draw is not pickable nor exportable.

params.name: view
params.desc: A View object where the method was invoked.

methods.example:
class ExampleOverlay < Sketchup::Overlay

  def initialize
    super('example_inc.my_overlay', 'Example Overlay')
  end

  def draw(view)
    # Draw a square.
    points = [
      Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0),
      Geom::Point3d.new(9, 0, 0),
      Geom::Point3d.new(9, 9, 0),
      Geom::Point3d.new(0, 9, 0)
    ]
    # Fill
    view.drawing_color = Sketchup::Color.new(255, 128, 128)
    view.draw(GL_QUADS, points)
    # Outline
    view.line_stipple = '' # Solid line
    view.drawing_color = Sketchup::Color.new(64, 0, 0)
    view.draw(GL_LINE_LOOP, points)
  end

end
notes: This is called very often. Perform minimal amount of computation in this event. Cache the data needed to draw what the overlay needs whenever possible.

If you draw outside the model bounds you need to implement Sketchup::Overlay#getExtents which return a bounding box large enough to include the points you draw. Otherwise your drawing will be clipped.

Sketchup::Pages.summary: The Pages class contains methods for manipulating a collection of Pages (Named "scenes" in the UI.) in a model. You get a handle to this collection by calling Model.pages.

methods.name: add_frame_change_observer
methods.summary: Class Methods The .add_frame_change_observer method is used to add a new frame change observer that is called with each frame of an animation, meaning the end user has clicked on a Scene tab (aka Page) inside SketchUp and the camera is animating to that scene. The method returns an integer id that can be stored and later used to remove the observer with the Sketchup::Pages.remove_frame_change_observer method.

params.name: object
params.desc: An object that implements the Sketchup::FrameChangeObserver#frameChange method.

returns.desc: A unique id of the observer

methods.example:
class MyFrameChangeObserver
  def frameChange(from_page, to_page, percent_done)
    puts "From page #{from_page.name} to #{to_page.name} (#{percent_done * 100}%)"
  end
end
id = Sketchup::Pages.add_frame_change_observer(MyFrameChangeObserver.new)

methods.name: remove_frame_change_observer
methods.summary: The .remove_frame_change_observer method is used to remove a frame change observer

params.name: observer_id
params.desc: The unique id returned by .add_frame_change_observer

methods.example: Sketchup::Pages.remove_frame_change_observer(id)

methods.summary: Instance Methods The [] method retrieves a page by either name or index.

params.name: index_or_name
params.desc: The index or the string name of the specific page.

returns.desc: page - a Page object if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
pages = model.pages
status = pages.add "Page 1"
status = pages.add "Page 2"
page = pages["Page 2"]

methods.name: add
signatures: add(name = nil, flags = PAGE_USE_ALL, index = self.size)
methods.summary: The #add method is used to add a new Page object to the collection. If no name is given, then a new name is generated using the default name for new Pages. If a name is given, then a new Page with that name is added. If the name is already used by another page, a unique name is created.

params.name: name
params.desc: The name of the specific page.

params.name: flags
params.desc: Bit flags in integer form.

params.name: index
params.desc: Index of where to inset.

bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2026.0 this method didn't make the name unique.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
pages = model.pages
status = pages.add "Page 1"
status = pages.add "Page 2"

methods.name: add_matchphoto_page
methods.summary: The #add_matchphoto_page method is used to add a photomatch page to the model. This is an advanced feature that was added to support internal SketchUp work, so it is unlikely to be useful to you.

params.name: image_filename
params.desc: The image file to use as the background.

methods.example:
pages = Sketchup.active_model.pages
page = pages.add_matchphoto_page("/path/to/image.png")

methods.name: add_observer
methods.summary: The add_observer method is used to add an observer to the Pages object. See the PagesObserver interface for more details.

params.name: observer
params.desc: An observer.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
pages = Sketchup.active_model.pages
status = pages.add_observer observer

methods.name: count
methods.example:
pages = Sketchup.active_model.pages
pages.add('Page 1')
pages.add('Page 2')
number = pages.count
notes: Since SketchUp 2014 the count method is inherited from Ruby's Enumerable mix-in module. Prior to that the #count method is an alias for #length.

methods.name: each
methods.summary: The #each method is used to iterate through pages in the model.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
pages = model.pages
pages.add("Page 1")
pages.add("Page 2")
pages.each { |page| puts page.name }

methods.name: erase
methods.summary: The #erase method is used to remove a page from the collection.
methods.example:
page = Sketchup.active_model.pages.add('Hello World')
Sketchup.active_model.pages.erase(page)

methods.name: length
methods.summary: The #length method is an alias for #size.
methods.example:
pages = Sketchup.active_model.pages
pages.add('Page 1')
pages.add('Page 2')
number = pages.length

methods.name: parent
methods.summary: The parent method is used to determine the model for the Pages collection.

returns.desc: model - the model that contains the pages if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
pages = model.pages
status = pages.add "Page 1"
status = pages.add "Page 2"
model = pages.parent

methods.name: remove_observer
methods.summary: The remove_observer method is used to remove an observer from the current object. See the PagesObserver interface for more details.

params.name: observer
params.desc: An observer.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
pages = Sketchup.active_model.pages
status = pages.remove_observer observer

methods.name: reorder
methods.summary: The #reorder method is used to reorder an existing Sketchup::Page object inside collection. new_index specifies the new position of the page. It should be a value between 0 and the max index of the Sketchup::Pages collection. Negative indices can be used to specify an index from the end of the list.

params.name: page
params.desc: The page to be reordered.

params.name: new_index
params.desc: Index of where to replace the page.

returns.desc: nil

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
pages = model.pages
pages.reorder(model.pages[0], 2)
raises: [IndexError] if the given new_index is out of range.

methods.name: selected_page
methods.summary: The selected_page method is used to retrieve the currently selected page.

returns.desc: page - the currently selected Page object if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
pages = model.pages
status = pages.add "Page 1"
status = pages.add "Page 2"
page = pages.selected_page

methods.name: selected_page=
methods.summary: The selected_page method is used to set the currently selected page. Once you set this, SketchUp will animate to that page as if the user had clicked on its scene tab.

returns.desc: status - true if successful

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
pages = model.pages
status = pages.add "Page 1"
status = pages.add "Page 2"
pages.selected_page = model.pages[1]

methods.name: show_frame_at
methods.summary: The #show_frame_at method is used to show a frame in animation (of the slide show) at a given time in seconds.

params.name: seconds
params.desc: The time in seconds.

returns.desc: Upon success it returns the page that is displayed and a parameter between 0.0 and 1.0 that is tells how far along the transition to next page you are at.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
pages = model.pages
pages.add("Page 1")
pages.add("Page 2")
page, ratio = pages.show_frame_at(1.8)
notes: In versions prior to SketchUp 2019 this method will crash if called when there are no pages in the model.

methods.name: size
methods.summary: The #size method is used to retrieve the number of pages.
methods.example:
pages = Sketchup.active_model.pages
pages.add('Page 1')
pages.add('Page 2')
number = pages.size

methods.name: slideshow_time
methods.summary: The slideshow_time method is used to get the amount of time that a slideshow of all of the pages will take. This takes into account the transition time for each Page and the amount of time that each Page is displayed.

returns.desc: status - true if successful

methods.example:
pages = Sketchup.active_model.pages
time = pages.slideshow_time

methods.name: unique_name
methods.summary: The #unique_name method is used to generate a unique name for the page based on a base_name string. For example, a base name of "Joe" might return "Joe 2" if "Joe" already exists.

params.name: base_name
params.desc: The base name to use for the unique name.

returns.desc: The unique name.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
pages = model.pages
page = pages.add('Joe')
page.unique_name('Joe')

Sketchup::PagesObserver.summary: This observer interface is implemented to react to pages events.

methods.name: onContentsModified
methods.summary: Instance Methods The #onContentsModified method is invoked whenever the pages change.

methods.name: onElementAdded
methods.summary: The #onElementAdded method is invoked when an element is added to a Sketchup::Pages object.

methods.name: onElementRemoved
methods.summary: The #onElementRemoved method is invoked when an element is removed from a Sketchup::Pages object.

Sketchup::PickHelper.summary: The Sketchup::PickHelper class is used to pick entities that reside under the current cursor location, similar to native Select tool. Unlike Sketchup::InputPoint, Sketchup::PickHelper uses no inference.

methods.name: all_picked
methods.summary: Instance Methods The all_picked method is used to get an array of entities from the active entities from all the pick paths. Duplicates might occur if there are multiple pick paths for entities that ends in a group or component.

returns.desc: elements - the array of elements in the pick.

methods.example:
ph = view.pick_helper
ph.do_pick(x, y)
entities = ph.all_picked

methods.name: best_picked
methods.summary: The best_picked method is used to retrieve the "best" entity picked (entity that you would have picked if you were using the select tool). Returns nil if nothing was picked. You must have called do_pick before calling this method.

returns.desc: entity - the best picked entity

methods.example:
ph = view.pick_helper
ph.do_pick(x, y)
best_entity = ph.best_picked

methods.name: boundingbox_pick
methods.summary: Used to pick a set of entities from a model from a Geom::BoundingBox. The pick criteria can be for completely-contained or partially-contained entities, similar to how the Selection tool works.

params.name: bounding_box
params.desc: Bounding box defining the volume to use for picking.

params.name: pick_type
params.desc: PICK_INSIDE to select entities completely contained or PICK_CROSSING to select entities partially contained.

params.name: transformation
params.desc: Transformation that will be applied to the volume defined by the bounding_box that allows for a rotation.

returns.desc: The number of entities picked

methods.example:
boundingbox = Geom::BoundingBox.new
boundingbox.add([1, 1, 1], [100, 100, 100])
ph = Sketchup.active_model.active_view.pick_helper

# Rotate the box 45' around the z-axis
angle = 45
transformation = Geom::Transformation.new(ORIGIN, Z_AXIS, angle)

num_picked = ph.boundingbox_pick(boundingbox, Sketchup::PickHelper::PICK_CROSSING,
  transformation)
if num_picked > 0
  Sketchup.active_model.selection.add(ph.all_picked)
end

methods.name: count
methods.summary: The count method is used to count the number of entities picked (number of pick records)

returns.desc: number - the number of entities picked

methods.example: number = pickhelper.count

methods.name: depth_at
methods.summary: The depth_at method retrieves the depth of one of the currently picked entities in the list of pick records.

params.name: index
params.desc: A number from 0 to number of items picked minus one.

returns.desc: integer - the depth of the entity if successful

methods.example:
pickhelper = view.pick_helper
pickhelper.do_pick(x, y)
# Iterate all pick-routes:
pickhelper.count.times { |pick_path_index|
  puts pickhelper.depth_at(pick_path_index)
}

methods.name: do_pick
methods.summary: The #do_pick method is used to perform the initial pick. This method is generally called before any other methods in the PickHelper class.

params.name: x
params.desc: Screen coordinate in physical pixels.

params.name: y
params.desc: Screen coordinate in physical pixels.

params.name: aperture
params.desc: The size of the aperture in physical pixels.

returns.desc: Number of entities picked.

methods.example:
ph = view.pick_helper
num = ph.do_pick(x, y)
entity = ph.best_picked
notes: Signature for versions prior to SketchUp 2025.0

methods.name: element_at
methods.summary: The element_at method is used to retrieve a specific entity in the list of picked elements. This element will be from the active entities. Use count() to get the number of possible pick paths.

params.name: index
params.desc: A number from 0 to number of items picked minus one.

returns.desc: entity - the entity at the index position in the list of picked entities.

methods.example:
pickhelper = view.pick_helper
pickhelper.do_pick(x, y)
# Iterate all pick-routes:
pickhelper.count.times { |pick_path_index|
  puts pickhelper.element_at(pick_path_index)
}
# You would iterate the same elements in all_picked.

methods.name: init
methods.summary: The #init method is used to initialize the PickHelper for testing points. You do not normally need to call this method, but you can use this if you want to call #test_point or #pick_segment on a lot of points.

params.name: x
params.desc: Screen coordinate in physical pixels.

params.name: y
params.desc: Screen coordinate in physical pixels.

params.name: aperture
params.desc: The size of the aperture in physical pixels. This is the width and height of the square picking aperture.

methods.example:
ph = view.pick_helper
ph.init(x, y, 5)
# Find all points picked by the screen click.
selected = points.select { |point|
  ph.test_point(point)
}
notes: Signature for versions prior to SketchUp 2025.0

methods.name: leaf_at
methods.summary: The leaf_at method retrieves the deepest thing in a pick path. For example, if you have a face that is within a component that is within another component, leaf_at returns the face. Use count() to get the number of possible pick paths.

params.name: index
params.desc: A number from 0 to number of items picked minus one.

returns.desc: entity - the leaf entity

methods.example:
pickhelper = view.pick_helper
pickhelper.do_pick(x, y)
# Iterate all pick-routes:
pickhelper.count.times { |pick_path_index|
  p pickhelper.leaf_at(pick_path_index)
}

methods.name: path_at
methods.summary: The path_at method is used to retrieve the entire path for an entity in the pick list (as an array). If one of the pick paths end in a face nested in a group nested in a component this method will return an array of these entities. The Group will be first and the face will be last.

params.name: index
params.desc: A number from 0 to number of items picked minus one.

returns.desc: array - an array of entities including the leaf

methods.example:
pickhelper = view.pick_helper
pickhelper.do_pick(x, y)
# Iterate all pick-routes:
pickhelper.count.times { |pick_path_index|
  p pickhelper.path_at(pick_path_index)
}

methods.name: pick_segment
methods.summary: The #pick_segment method is used to pick a segment of a polyline curve that is defined by an array of points. If you click on a point in a polyline curve, the index of the point in the curve is returned (starting at 0).

params.name: points
params.desc: A series of points in the polyline as a list of parameters or an array containing Point3d objects.

params.name: x
params.desc: screen mouse position in pixels.

params.name: y
params.desc: (required if x given) screen mouse position in pixels.

params.name: aperture
params.desc: aperture in pixels.

returns.desc: an index on success, false on failure

methods.example:
point1 = Geom::Point3d.new(0 ,0, 0)
point2 = Geom::Point3d.new(10, 0, 0)
segment = [point1, point2]
ph = view.pick_helper
# If testing many points this is the fastest way to test.
ph.init(x, y)
picked = ph.pick_segment(segment)
# This do not require .init
picked = ph.pick_segment(segment, x, y)
notes: The return value will be a negative index when a segment is picked.

methods.name: picked_edge
methods.summary: The picked_edge method is used to retrieve the "best" Edge picked. Returns nil if there were no edges picked. You must have called do_pick before calling this method.

returns.desc: edge - an Edge object if successful

methods.example:
ph = view.pick_helper
ph.do_pick(x, y)
edge = ph.picked_edge

methods.name: picked_element
methods.summary: The picked_element method retrieves the best drawing element, that is not an edge or a face, picked. Returns nil if nothing was picked. You must have called do_pick before calling this method.

returns.desc: a drawing element that is not an edge or face

methods.example:
ph = view.pick_helper
ph.do_pick(x, y)
entity = ph.picked_element

methods.name: picked_face
methods.summary: The picked_face method is used to retrieve the best face picked. Returns nil if there were no faces picked. You must have called do_pick before calling this method.

returns.desc: face - a Face object if successful

methods.example:
ph = view.pick_helper
ph.do_pick(x, y)
face = ph.picked_face

methods.name: test_point
methods.summary: The #test_point method is used to test a point to see if it would be selected using the default or given pick aperture. There is no need to invoke #do_pick for this and the results are unrelated.

params.name: point
params.desc: Model coordinate.

params.name: x
params.desc: X screen coordinate for the pick.

params.name: y
params.desc: Y screen coordinate for the pick.

params.name: aperture
params.desc: aperture in pixels.

methods.example:
ph = view.pick_helper
# If testing many points this is the fastest way to test.
ph.init(x, y)
picked = ph.test_point(point)
# These do not require init()
picked = ph.test_point(point, x, y)
picked = ph.test_point(point, x, y, aperture)

methods.name: transformation_at
methods.summary: The transformation_at method is used to get a transformation at a specific pick path index in the pick helper. The transformation combines the transformation of all groups, components and images in the pick path. This transformation can be used to transform the coordinates of the leaf entity into the coordinates of the active entities.

params.name: index
params.desc: The index where the transformation should be retrieved.

returns.desc: transformation - the transformation found

methods.example:
pickhelper = view.pick_helper
pickhelper.do_pick(x, y)
# Iterate all pick-routes:
pickhelper.count.times { |pick_path_index|
  puts pickhelper.transformation_at(pick_path_index)
}

methods.name: view
methods.summary: The #view method is used to get the view associated with the Sketchup::PickHelper.
methods.example:
view = Sketchup.active_model.active_view
ph = view.pick_helper
ph.view

methods.name: window_pick
methods.summary: Used to pick a set of entities from a model based on a screen coordinate rectangular area defined by two points. The pick criteria can be for completely-contained or partially-contained entities, similar to how the Selection tool works. The z value of the points passed in are ignored.

params.name: start_point
params.desc: First screen coordinate point.

params.name: end_point
params.desc: Second screen coordinate point.

params.name: pick_type
params.desc: PICK_INSIDE to select entities completely contained or PICK_CROSSING to select entities partially contained.

returns.desc: The number of Sketchup::Drawingelement objects picked.

methods.example:
ph = Sketchup.active_model.active_view.pick_helper
start_point = Geom::Point3d.new(100, 100, 0)
end_point = Geom::Point3d.new(500, 500, 0)
num_picked = ph.window_pick(start_point, end_point, Sketchup::PickHelper::PICK_CROSSING)
picked_entities = ph.all_picked
notes: Prior to SketchUp 2025.0 this method expected physical screen coordinates. As of SketchUp 2025.0 they are expected to be logical screen coordinates.

Sketchup::RegionalSettings.summary: The Sketchup::RegionalSettings module contains methods getting information about the user's locale settings. Note that when you convert between units and strings you don't need to parse it yourself and you can instead use String#to_l and Length#to_s.

methods.name: decimal_separator
methods.summary: Class Methods Returns the decimal character for the current user's locale.

returns.desc: the decimal separator character

methods.example:
# Format a Float using the user's locale settings.
# Ruby's Float.to_s always use period as decimal separator.
formatted = 0.123.to_s.tr('.', Sketchup::RegionalSettings.decimal_separator)

methods.name: list_separator
methods.summary: Returns the list separator character for the current user's locale.

returns.desc: the list separator character

methods.example:
# Format a CSV list in user's locale:
decimal = Sketchup::RegionalSettings.decimal_separator
list = Sketchup::RegionalSettings.list_separator
row = [3.14, 1.618, 2.718]
csv = row.map { |value| value.to_s.tr('.', decimal) }.join(list)

Sketchup::RenderingOptions.summary: The RenderingOptions class contains method to extract the rendering information for a model. The majority of the rendering information returned exists in the Styles dialog. The following rendering information keys are maintained in SketchUp:

methods.name: each_key
methods.summary: Class Methods The #each_key method iterates through all of the rendering options keys.

methods.name: keys
methods.summary: The keys method returns an array with all of the attribute keys.

returns.desc: an array of keys

methods.example: keys = Sketchup.active_model.rendering_options.keys

methods.summary: Instance Methods The #[] method is used to get the value of a rendering option.

params.name: key
params.desc: The key of the rendering option value to get.

methods.example: result = Sketchup.active_model.rendering_options["DisplayInstanceAxes"]

methods.summary: The set value []= method is used to set the value in the array of rendering options.

params.name: key
params.desc: The key of the rendering option value to set.

params.name: value
params.desc: The value to be set.

returns.desc: the value that was set

methods.example: Sketchup.active_model.rendering_options["DisplayInstanceAxes"] = false
raises: [ArgumentError] If the given key is invalid, the key's value is not settable, or the given value is invalid. SketchUp versions earlier than 2024.0 will not raise this error.

methods.name: add_observer
methods.summary: The add_observer method is used to add an observer to the current object.

params.name: observer
params.desc: An observer.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
observer = Sketchup::RenderingOptionsObserver.new # Dummy observer.
result = Sketchup.active_model.rendering_options.add_observer(observer)

methods.name: count
methods.summary: The #count method is inherited from the Enumerable mix-in module.
methods.example:
options = Sketchup.active_model.rendering_options
number = options.count

methods.name: each
methods.summary: The #each method iterates through all of the rendering options key/value pairs.

methods.name: each_key
methods.summary: The #each_key method iterates through all of the rendering options keys.

methods.name: each_pair
methods.summary: The #each_pair method is an alias for #each.

methods.name: keys
methods.summary: The keys method returns an array with all of the attribute keys.

returns.desc: an array of keys

methods.example: keys = Sketchup.active_model.rendering_options.keys

methods.name: length
methods.summary: The #length method returns the number of options in the rendering options collection.
methods.example:
options = Sketchup.active_model.rendering_options
number = options.length

methods.name: remove_observer
methods.summary: The remove_observer method is used to remove an observer from the current object.

Sketchup::SectionPlane.summary: The SectionPlane class represents a section plane in a SketchUp model. Note that prior to SketchUp 2014 there was no way to create a SectionPlane object using Ruby. For older versions of SketchUp, you must manually create a section plane with the Section Plane Tool in SketchUp and then query the entities array to find the SectionPlane object.

methods.name: activate
methods.summary: Instance Methods The activate method is used to make the section plane the active one of its parent component/group.

methods.example:
entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities

entities = Sketchup.active_model.entities

methods.name: get_plane

model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities

sp = entities.grep(Sketchup::SectionPlane).first
plane = sp.get_plane
if (plane)

end

model = Sketchup.active_model

model = Sketchup.active_model

model = Sketchup.active_model

Sketchup::Selection.summary: A set of the currently selected drawing elements. Use the Model.selection method to get a Selection object. Note that the order of drawing elements (selection[0], selection[1] and so on) in the set is in no particular order and should not be assumed to be in the same order as the user selected the drawing elements.

methods.summary: Instance Methods The #[] method is used to retrieve a Sketchup::Drawingelement from the selection by index. Index 0 is the first Drawingelement in the selection. This method is not very efficient. If you need to look at every entity in the selection, consider using #each instead of using this method to manually grab each one.

params.name: index
params.desc: The index of the Drawingelement object to retrieve.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
selection = model.selection
selection.add(entities.to_a)
p selection[0]

returns.desc: the number of Drawingelement objects added

methods.example:
# Add by listing the Drawingelements...
ss.add(e1, e2, e3)

# ...or add by passing an Array of Drawingelements.
ss.add([e1, e2, e3])

methods.name: add_observer
methods.summary: The add_observer method is used to add an observer to the selection object.

params.name: observer
params.desc: An observer.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
selection = Sketchup.active_model.selection
status = selection.add_observer observer

methods.name: at
methods.summary: The #at method is an alias for #[].

params.name: index
params.desc: The index of the Drawingelement object to retrieve.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
selection = model.selection
selection.add(entities.to_a)
p selection.at(0)

methods.name: clear
methods.summary: The clear method is used to clear the selection.
methods.example:
entity = entities[0]
selection.add entity
UI.messagebox "Ready to Clear"
selection.clear

methods.name: contains?
methods.summary: The #contains? method is and alias of #include?.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entity = model.active_entities.first
selection = model.selection
selection.add(entity)
p selection.contains?(entity)

methods.name: count
methods.example:
selection = Sketchup.active_model.selection
number = selection.count
notes: Since SketchUp 2014 the count method is inherited from Ruby's Enumerable mix-in module. Prior to that the #count method is an alias for #length.

methods.name: each
methods.summary: The #each method is used to iterate through all of the selected Drawingelements. If you want to do something with all of the selected Drawingelements, this is more efficient than using #[].
methods.example: selection.each { |drawing_element| puts drawing_element }
notes: Don't remove content from this collection while iterating over it with #each. This would change the size of the collection and cause elemnts to be skipped as the indices change. Instead copy the ...

methods.name: empty?
methods.summary: The #empty? method is used to determine if there are drawing elements in the selection.
methods.example:
status = selection.add drawing_element
status = selection.empty

methods.name: first
methods.summary: The #first method is used to retrieve the first selected Drawingelement Returns nil if nothing is selected. This method is useful when you know that only a single Drawingelement is selected, or you are only interested in the first selected Drawingelement.

returns.desc: the first selected Drawingelement object if successful

methods.example:
status = selection.add drawing_element
drawing_element = selection.first

methods.name: include?
methods.summary: The #include? method is used to determine if a given Sketchup::Drawingelement is in the selection.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entity = model.active_entities.first
selection = model.selection
selection.add(entity)
p selection.include?(entity)

methods.name: invert
methods.summary: The #invert method is used to invert the selection.
methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
selection = model.selection
# Create a cube
face = entities.add_face([0, 0, 0], [9, 0, 0], [9, 9, 0], [0, 9, 0])
face.pushpull(-9)
# Add the first two faces to the selection
faces = entities.grep(Sketchup::Face).take(2)
selection.add(faces)
# Invert selection
selection.invert

methods.name: is_curve?
methods.summary: The #is_curve? method is used to determine if the selection contains all edges that belong to a single curve.
methods.example:
selection.add drawing_element
status = selection.is_curve?

methods.name: is_surface?
methods.summary: The #is_surface? method is used to determine if the selection contains only all of the faces that are part of a single curved surface.
methods.example:
selection.add drawing_element
status = selection.is_surface

methods.name: length
methods.summary: The #length method is used to retrieve the number of selected drawing elements.
methods.example:
selection = Sketchup.active_model.selection
number = selection.length

methods.name: model
methods.summary: The #model method retrieves the model for the selection.

returns.desc: the model that includes the selection if successful

methods.example: model = selection.model

methods.name: nitems
methods.summary: The #nitems method is an alias for #length.
methods.example:
selection = Sketchup.active_model.selection
number = selection.nitems

methods.name: remove
methods.summary: The #remove method is used to remove Drawingelements from the selection. You can pass it individual Drawingelements or an Array of Drawingelements.

returns.desc: the number of Drawingelement objects removed

methods.example:
# Remove by listing the Drawingelements...
ss.remove(e1, e2, e3)

# ...or remove by passing an Array of Drawingelements.
ss.remove([e1, e2, e3])

methods.name: remove_observer
methods.summary: The remove_observer method is used to remove an observer from the selection object.

params.name: observer
params.desc: An observer.

returns.desc: true if successful, false if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
selection = Sketchup.active_model.selection
status = object.remove_observer observer

methods.name: shift
methods.summary: The #shift method is used to remove the first Drawingelement from the selection and returns it.

returns.desc: the first Drawingelement object in the selection set if successful

methods.example:
status = selection.add drawing_element
UI.messagebox "Ready to remove item from selection set"
drawing_element = selection.shift

methods.name: single_object?
methods.summary: The #single_object? method is used to determine if the selection contains a single object. It can either be a single DrawingElement or a group of DrawingElements for which is_curve? or is_surface? will return true.
methods.example: status = selection.single_object

methods.name: size
methods.summary: The #size method is an alias for #length.
methods.example:
selection = Sketchup.active_model.selection
number = selection.size

methods.name: toggle
methods.summary: The #toggle method is used to change whether a Drawingelement is part of the selection. Drawingelements that are not already selected are added. Drawingelements that are already selected are removed. You can pass it individual Drawingelements or an Array of Drawingelements.

returns.desc: the number of Drawingelement objects changed

methods.example:
# Toggle by listing the Drawingelements...
ss.toggle(e1, e2, e3)

# ...or toggle by passing an Array of Drawingelements.
ss.toggle([e1, e2, e3])

Sketchup::SelectionObserver.summary: This observer interface is implemented to react to selection events.

methods.name: onSelectionAdded
methods.summary: Instance Methods
notes: This event might not trigger even if a single element is selected. For instance the Selection tool will trigger #onSelectionBulkChange regardless.

methods.name: onSelectionBulkChange
methods.summary: The #onSelectionBulkChange method is called whenever items are added or removed from the selection set. The #onSelectionBulkChange callback will not trigger if the selection is cleared by clicking on empty model space. Use the #onSelectionCleared method to catch this case.

methods.name: onSelectionCleared
methods.summary: The #onSelectionCleared method is called when the selection is completely emptied.

methods.name: onSelectionRemoved
bugs: Due to a bug in SketchUp this event doesn't trigger. Instead onSelectedRemoved is called.
methods.example:
class MySelectionObserver < Sketchup::SelectionObserver
 def onSelectionRemoved(selection, entity)
   puts "onSelectionRemoved: #{entity}"
 end

 # Due to a SketchUp bug, this method is called by the wrong name.
 alias_method :onSelectedRemoved, :onSelectionRemoved
end

# Attach the observer.
Sketchup.active_model.selection.add_observer(MySelectionObserver.new)
notes: This event might not trigger even if a single element is deselected. For instance the Selection tool will trigger #onSelectionBulkChange regardless.

Sketchup::Set.summary: The set class represents a collection of unique objects. Sketchup::ShadowInfo.summary: The Sketchup::ShadowInfo class contains method to extract the shadow information for a model. Sketchup::Skp.summary: The Sketchup::Skp module is used to read metadata from external SketchUp files without loading the whole file.

Sketchup::Snap.summary: A Snap is a custom grip used by SketchUp's Move tool. Snaps can be added at strategic places such as connectors to help assembling objects. rdoc-image:../images/snaps.png #direction is the direction a snap is "pointing". This can be thought of as the normal direction of the snap. It can also be thought of as the direction you move an object when plugging it into another object, e.g. inserting a power coord.

methods.name: direction
methods.summary: Instance Methods The #direction method is used to get the direction this Snap is "pointing". When two Snaps are snapped into each other, they have the opposite #direction.
methods.example:

direction = snap.direction

snap = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_snap(ORIGIN)

snap = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_snap(ORIGIN)

methods.name: up
methods.summary: The #up method is used to get a vector representing the rotation of this Snap along its axis. When two Snaps are snapped into each other, they have the same aligned #up direction.
methods.example:
snap = Sketchup.active_model.entities.add_snap(ORIGIN)
up = snap.up

Sketchup::Texture.summary: The Texture class contains methods for obtaining information about textures that are part of your materials in your model (within the In-Model section of the Materials Browser). Remember, textures are repeatable images that "tile" when painted on a surface.

methods.name: average_color
methods.summary: Instance Methods The average_color method retrieves a color object with the average color found in the texture.

returns.desc: a color object (if successful), nil if unsuccessful.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
materials=model.materials
# Adds a material as an in model material
m = materials.add "Test Color"
begin
  # Returns nil if not successful, path if successful
  m.texture = "c:\\Materials\\Carpet.jpg"
rescue
  puts $!.message
end
texture = m.texture
# Returns a color object
color = texture.average_color

methods.name: filename
methods.summary: The #filename method retrieves the full path, if available, for a texture object. Textures for materials shipping with SketchUp might only have a filename, since the path would be invalid on the end user's machine. Textures dynamically created from ImageRep objects may have an empty path unless saved with Sketchup::ImageRep#save_file or until the texture is saved with Sketchup::Texture#write.

returns.desc: a string representation of the path and filename used for the texture.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
materials = model.materials
material = materials.add("Test Color")
material.texture = "c:\\Materials\\Carpet.jpg"
texture = material.texture
filename = texture.filename
notes: Since SketchUp 2021.0 this method will append a file extension matching the image format if the file extension is missing from stored filepath.

methods.name: height
methods.summary: The height method is used to get the height of a repeatable texture image, in inches.

returns.desc: the height, in inches, of the texture pattern

methods.example: height = texture.height

methods.name: image_height
methods.summary: The image_height method retrieves the height of the repeatable texture image, in pixels.

returns.desc: the height, in pixels, of the texture pattern

methods.example: imageheight = texture.image_height

methods.name: image_rep
methods.summary: The #image_rep method returns a copy of a Sketchup::ImageRep object representing the texture pixel data.

params.name: colorized
params.desc: Set to true to obtain the colorized version.

methods.example:
texture = Sketchup.active_model.materials[0].texture
image_rep = texture.image_rep

methods.name: image_width
methods.summary: The image_width method retrieves the width of the repeatable texture image, in pixels.

returns.desc: the width, in pixels, of the texture pattern

methods.example: imagewidth = texture.image_width

methods.name: size=
methods.summary: The size= method allows you to set the size of the repeatable texture image, in inches,

params.name: size
params.desc: The size, in inches, of the texture. This number will apply to height and width to keep aspect ratio. You can also pass as a parameter an array of two numeric values which will set width and height ...

returns.desc: the size, in inches, of the texture. This number will apply to height and width to keep aspect ratio. If you have passed in an array of two numbers for width and height, the same array will be returned if successful.

methods.example:
size = texture.size = 60
imagewidth = texture.width

if (imagewidth)
  puts imagewidth
else
  puts "Failure"
end

# Using two values which will not preserve ratio
width_height = texture.size = [10,100]

methods.name: width

returns.desc: the width, in inches, of the texture pattern

methods.example: width = texture.width

methods.name: write
methods.summary: Writes the texture to file with option to preserve the color adjustments made by the material.

params.name: path
params.desc: The file path to write the texture to.

params.desc: Boolean - Allows for the texture to be exported with the color adjustments.

returns.desc: true if the method succeeded

material = Sketchup.active_model.materials[0]

Sketchup::TextureWriter.summary: The TextureWriter class is used primarily for writing the textures used in a SketchUp model out to files as part of an export for use in another application. These methods are usually invoked in this order: 1. #load - load one or more textures from a model into the TextureWriter. 2. #write_all or #write - write the texture(s) to file.

methods.name: count
methods.summary: Instance Methods The #length method is used to determine the number of textures loaded into the texture writer. The #count method is an alias for #length.

returns.desc: length - the number of textures loaded in the texture writer

methods.example:
length = tw.length
tw.load(texturable_entities[0])
if length < tw.length
  puts("A new entity was successfully loaded into the writer.")
end

methods.name: filename
methods.summary: The filename method is used to retrieve the original filename for a particular texture.

params.name: handle
params.desc: The index or handle of the texture in the texture writer.

returns.desc: filename - the filename of the texture on the file system. Textures can be generated without filenames, so if the texture doesn't have a name write_all will save the texture to an image file named "i.png". Where i is the first integer greater than zero which was not already used for a png file name.

methods.example:
index = tw.load(texturable_entities[0])
filename = tw.filename(index)
puts("filename = #{filename}")

methods.name: handle
methods.summary: The handle method is used to retrieve a handle or index for a specific texture in the texture writer.

params.name: entity
params.desc: A image, component instance, group, or layer.

params.name: side
params.desc: Specifies one of the sides of the face (true if front, false if back.)

returns.desc: the index for the entity in the texture writer.

methods.example:
tw.load(texturable_entities[0])
handle = tw.handle(texturable_entities[0])

methods.name: length
methods.summary: The #length method is used to determine the number of textures loaded into the texture writer. The #count method is an alias for #length.

returns.desc: length - the number of textures loaded in the texture writer

methods.example:
length = tw.length
tw.load(texturable_entities[0])
if length < tw.length
  puts("A new entity was successfully loaded into the writer.")
end

methods.name: load
methods.summary: The load method is used to load one or more textures into the texture writer for writing out to a file.

params.name: entity
params.desc: Image, component instance, group, or layer to load.

params.name: face
params.desc: A face to load.

params.name: side
params.desc: A boolean used to indicate the side of the face being loaded (true if front, false if back).

returns.desc: handle - the index or handle of the entity that was loaded

methods.example: index = tw.load(texturable_entities[0])
notes: If you are passing a face in as the entity argument when loading a texture you will have to specify the second boolean argument, side. The argument side specifies which side of the face the texture ...

methods.name: write
methods.summary: The write method is used to write an individual textures, within the texture writer, to a file. An entity's texture must have been loaded into the texture writer before this method can be used to write it's texture. This method will return one of the following status messages. (These are constants that are defined by the API.)

params.name: entity
params.desc: An image, component instance, group, or layer to write.

params.name: filename
params.desc: The name of the file to contain the texture.

params.name: side
params.desc: A boolean used to indicate the side of the face being written (true if front, false if back).

returns.desc: status - one of three status messages (see comments.)

methods.example:
tw.load(texturable_entities[0])
if tw.write(texturable_entities[0], "C:\\textures\\A.jpg") == FILE_WRITE_OK
  puts("JPEG file successfully written.")
end
notes: If you are passing a face in as the entity argument when writing a texture you will have to specify the boolean argument, side. The argument side controls the side of the face from which the texture ...

methods.name: write_all
methods.summary: The write_all method is used to write all of the textures within the texture writer to files. It will return one of three status numbers: - 0 = FILE_WRITE_OK - 1 = FILE_WRITE_FAILED_INVALID_TYPE - 2 = FILE_WRITE_FAILED_UNKNOWN

params.name: dirname
params.desc: The directory to write to.

params.name: filename_format
params.desc: true to use 8.3 DOS name format.

returns.desc: status - one of three status messages (see comments.)

methods.example:
tw.load(texturable_entities[0]
tw.load(faces[0], false)
if tw.write_all("C:\\textures\\", true) == FILE_WRITE_OK
  puts("Texture files were successfully written.")
end

Sketchup::Tool.summary: Tool is the interface that you implement to create a SketchUp tool. See code example[https://github.com/SketchUp/sketchup-ruby-api-tutorials/tree/main/examples/02_custom_tool] for how to create a custom tool in Ruby.

methods.name: activate
methods.summary: Instance Methods The #activate method is called by SketchUp when the tool is selected. It is a good place to put most of your initialization, such as instance variables to track the state of the tool.
methods.example:
def activate
  puts 'Your tool has been activated.'
end

methods.name: deactivate
methods.summary: The #deactivate method is called when the tool is deactivated because a different tool was selected.

methods.name: draw
methods.summary: The #draw method is called by SketchUp whenever the view is refreshed to allow the tool to do its own drawing. If the tool has some temporary graphics that it wants displayed while it is active, it should implement this method and draw to the Sketchup::View.

params.name: view
params.desc: A View object where the method was invoked.

methods.example:
def draw(view)
  # Draw a square.
  points = [
    Geom::Point3d.new(0, 0, 0),
    Geom::Point3d.new(9, 0, 0),
    Geom::Point3d.new(9, 9, 0),
    Geom::Point3d.new(0, 9, 0)
  ]
  # Fill
  view.drawing_color = Sketchup::Color.new(255, 128, 128)
  view.draw(GL_QUADS, points)
  # Outline
  view.line_stipple = '' # Solid line
  view.drawing_color = Sketchup::Color.new(64, 0, 0)
  view.draw(GL_LINE_LOOP, points)
end
notes: If you draw outside the model bounds you need to implement Tool#getExtents which return a bounding box large enough to include the points you draw. Otherwise your drawing will be clipped.

methods.name: enableVCB?
methods.summary: The #enableVCB? method is used to tell SketchUp whether to allow the user to enter text into the VCB (value control box, aka the "measurements" panel). If you do not implement this method, then the vcb is disabled by default.

returns.desc: Return true if you want the VCB enabled

methods.example:
# For this tool, allow vcb text entry while the tool is active.
def enableVCB?
  return true
end

methods.name: getExtents
methods.summary: In order to accurately draw things, SketchUp needs to know the extents of what it is drawing. If the tool is doing its own drawing, it may need to implement this method to tell SketchUp the extents of what it will be drawing. If you don't implement this method, you may find that part of what the tool is drawing gets clipped to the extents of the rest of the model.
methods.example:
def getExtents
  bb = Sketchup.active_model.bounds
  return bb
end

methods.name: getInstructorContentDirectory
methods.summary: The #getInstructorContentDirectory method is used to tell SketchUp the directory containing your Tool's instructor content. To use this, create a custom instructor directory, put an index.html file inside of it, and then return that path via this method. If the SketchUp user has the Instructor window open when they activate your tool, they will see your html file.

returns.desc: the directory path where the Instructor content exists.

methods.example:
def getInstructorContentDirectory
  extension_path = Sketchup.extensions['MyExtension].extension_path
  instructor_path = File.join(extension_path, 'MyExtension', 'instructor')
  return instructor_path
end
notes: Prior to SketchUp 2014 this method would assume the path was relative to the SketchUp resource folder. From 2014 and onwards you can specify the absolute path to an HTML file or the absolute path to ...

methods.name: getMenu
methods.summary: The #getMenu method is called by SketchUp to let the tool provide its own context menu. Most tools will not want to implement this method and, instead, use the normal context menu found on all entities. If you do implement this method, the argument is a Menu. You should use the Sketchup::Menu#add_item method to build the context menu.

params.name: flags
params.desc: A bit mask that tells the state of the modifier keys and other mouse buttons at the time.

params.name: x
params.desc: Screen coordinate in physical pixels.

params.name: y
params.desc: Screen coordinate in physical pixels.

methods.example:
if Sketchup.version.to_i < 15
  # Compatible with SketchUp 2014 and older:
  def getMenu(menu)
    menu.add_item('Say Hello') {
      UI.messagebox('Hello')
    }
  end
else
  # Only works with SketchUp 2015 and newer:
  def getMenu(menu, flags, x, y, view)
    ph = view.pick_helper(x, y)
    entity = ph.best_picked
    if entity
      view.model.selection.clear
      view.model.selection.add(entity)
      menu.add_item("Erase #{entity.typename}") {
        entity.erase!
      }
   end
 end
end
notes: In SketchUp 2015 the flags, x, y and view parameters were added. They are needed if you need to pick the entities under the mouse position. The new parameters are optional, but if you need to use one ...
Signature for versions prior to SketchUp 2025.0

methods.name: onCancel
methods.summary: The #onCancel method is called by SketchUp to cancel the current operation of the tool. The typical response will be to reset the tool to its initial state. The reason identifies the action that triggered the call. The reason can be one of the following values:

params.name: reason
params.desc: A reason value (see comments).

notes: When something is undone #onCancel is called before the undo is actually executed. If you need to do something with the model after an undo use Sketchup::ModelObserver#onTransactionUndo.
When #onKeyDown is implemented and returns true, pressing Esc doesn't trigger #onCancel.

methods.name: onKeyDown
methods.summary: The #onKeyDown method is called by SketchUp when the user presses a key on the keyboard. If you want to get input from the VCB, you should implement onUserText rather than this method. This method is can be used for special keys such as the Shift key, Ctrl key, and so on, or for just determining which key a user pressed. This method is actually called for all keys that are pressed.

params.name: key
params.desc: The key that was pressed.

params.name: repeat
params.desc: A value of 1 for a single press of a key. A value of 2 if the user has pressed a key and is holding it down.

params.name: flags
params.desc: A bit mask that tells the state of the modifier keys at the time of the event.

returns.desc: Return true to prevent SketchUp from processing the event.

bugs: SketchUp 2026.0 (Windows) introduced a regression in Sketchup::Tool#onKeyDown where the event didn't trigger when Return/Enter was pressed. This was fixed in SketchUp 2026.1.
methods.example:
def onKeyDown(key, repeat, flags, view)
  puts "onKeyDown: key = #{key}"
  puts "        repeat = #{repeat}"
  puts "         flags = #{flags}"
  puts "          view = #{view}"
end

methods.name: onKeyUp
methods.summary: The #onKeyUp method is called by SketchUp when the user releases a key on the keyboard.

params.name: key
params.desc: The key that was pressed.

params.name: repeat

params.name: flags

end

methods.name: onActiveToolChanged
methods.summary: Instance Methods Once you subclass Sketchup::ToolsObserver with your unique class, you can override the #onActiveToolChanged method to receive tool change notifications.

params.name: tools
params.desc: A Tools object.

params.name: tool_name
params.desc: The name of the tool.

params.name: tool_id
params.desc: The ID of the tool. This is a predefined number unique to a given tool. For example, the Materials Browser is tool_id 21074.

methods.example:
def onActiveToolChanged(tools, tool_name, tool_id)
  tool_name = fix_mac_tool_name(tool_name)
  puts "onActiveToolChanged: #{tool_name}"
end

# Returns the "correct" tool name to account for mac API differences.
#
#   Args:
#     tool_name     The tool name to fix
#
#   Returns
#     string   corrected tool name
def fix_mac_tool_name(tool_name)
  if tool_name == "eTool"
    tool_name = "ScaleTool"
  elsif tool_name == "ool"
    tool_name = "MoveTool"
  elsif tool_name == "onentCSTool"
    tool_name = "ComponentCSTool"
  elsif tool_name == "PullTool"
    tool_name = "PushPullTool"
  end
  return tool_name
end
notes: In SketchUp 6 and SketchUp 7.0, tool names on the Mac have some of their first characters truncated. For instance, on Windows, a tool is "CameraOrbit". On the Mac, is comes across as "raOrbit". ...

Sketchup::UVHelper.summary: The UV Helper class contains methods allowing you to determine the location (UV coordinates) of a texture on a face. This class is particularly useful in determining how textures that have been manipulated using the Texture Tweaker should appear when exported to another file type Use the Face.get_UVHelper method to create a UVHelper for a given face. See the TextureWriter class as well.

methods.name: get_back_UVQ
methods.summary: Instance Methods The #get_back_UVQ method is used to get the UV texture coordinates on the back of a face.

params.name: point
params.desc: A point on the face.

returns.desc: Point where X represents U, Y represents V and Z represents Q.

methods.example:
uv_helper = face.get_UVHelper(true, true, my_texture_writer)
face.outer_loop.vertices.each do |vert|
  uvq = uv_helper.get_back_UVQ(vert.position)
  # "Normalize" UVQ to UV.
  # #x, #y and #z corresponds to U, V and Q respectively,
  # as SketchUp re-uses the normal Point3d objects for UVQs
  u = uvq.x / uvq.z
  v = uvq.y / uvq.z
  puts "u=#{u} v=#{v}""
end
notes: To convert UVQ coordinates to UV, divide U and V by Q. u = uvq.u / uvq.q v = uvq.v / uvq.q

methods.name: get_front_UVQ
methods.summary: The #get_front_UVQ method is used to get the UV texture coordinates on the front of a face.

params.name: point
params.desc: A point on the face.

returns.desc: Point where X represents U, Y represents V and Z represents Q.

methods.example:
uv_helper = face.get_UVHelper(true, true, my_texture_writer)
face.outer_loop.vertices.each do |vert|
  uvq = uv_helper.get_front_UVQ(vert.position)
  # "Normalize" UVQ to UV.
  # #x, #y and #z corresponds to U, V and Q respectively,
  # as SketchUp re-uses the normal Point3d objects for UVQs
  u = uvq.x / uvq.z
  v = uvq.y / uvq.z
  puts "u=#{u} v=#{v}""
end
notes: To convert UVQ coordinates to UV, divide U and V by Q. u = uvq.u / uvq.q v = uvq.v / uvq.q

Sketchup::Vertex.summary: A Vertex. A Vertex represents the end of an Edge or a point inside a Face.

methods.name: common_edge
methods.summary: Instance Methods The common_edge method is used to find a common edge that is defined by this vertex and another vertex

params.name: vertex2
params.desc: A Vertex object.

returns.desc: an Edge object common to both vertices if successful. Returns nil if there is no edge between the two vertices.

methods.example:
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.active_entities
edge = entities.add_line([0, 0, 0], [20, 20, 20], [40, 40, 40])

# returns array of vertices that make up the line
vertices = edge.vertices
vertex1 = vertices[0]
vertex2 = vertices[1]

methods.name: curve_interior?
methods.summary: The #curve_interior? method is used to determine if this vertex is on the interior of a Curve.
methods.example:
centerpoint = Geom::Point3d.new
# Create a circle perpendicular to the normal or Z axis
vector = Geom::Vector3d.new(0, 0, 1)
vector2 = vector.normalize!
model = Sketchup.active_model
entities = model.entities
edgearray = entities.add_circle(ORIGIN, Z_AXIS, 10)
edge = edgearray[0]
curve = edge.curve
vertices = curve.vertices
# returns array of vertices that make up the circle
vertices = edge.vertices
vertex1 = vertices[0]
status = vertex1.curve_interior?
notes: This method doesn't actually return a boolean as the question mark post-fix would normally indicate. But the result still evaluates to truthy or falsy.

methods.summary: This method is used to draw text on the screen and is usually invoked within the draw method of a tool. The TextVerticalAlignCenter option will align the text to the center of the height of the first line, not the whole boundingbox of the text. To align around the full bounds of the text, use #text_bounds to compute the desired alignment.

params.name: point
params.desc: A Point3d object representing a 2D coordinate in view space.

methods.example:
class ExampleTool
  def draw(view)
    # This works in all SketchUp versions and draws the text using the
    # default font, size and color (i.e. the model edge color).
    point = Geom::Point3d.new(200, 100, 0)
    view.draw_text(point, "This is a test")

    # This works in SketchUp 2016 and up.
    options = {
      :font => "Arial",
      :size => 20,
      :bold => true,
      :align => TextAlignRight
    }
    point = Geom::Point3d.new(200, 200, 0)
    view.draw_text(point, "This is another\ntest", options)

    # You can also use Ruby 2.0's named arguments:
    point = Geom::Point3d.new(200, 200, 0)
    view.draw_text(point, "Hello world!", color: "Red")
  end
end
notes: Under Windows the font name must be less than 32 characters - due to system limitations.
As of SU2017 this will automatically scale the font-size by the same factor as UI.scale_factor.

UI::HtmlDialog.summary: The Ruby HtmlDialog class allows you to create and interact with HTML dialog boxes from Ruby. This is the best way to generate complex, embedded UIs inside SketchUp, but it does generally require HTML and JavaScript expertise. If your goal is to simple display a website to your users, consider using UI#openURL, which will show them a web page in their default browser rather than inside a dialog in SketchUp.

methods.name: add_action_callback
methods.summary: Instance Methods The #add_action_callback method establishes a Ruby callback method that your html dialog can call to perform some function. Use the sketchup.callback_method_name to invoke the callback method from your html dialog. Your JavaScript in the html dialog will invoke the callback with the same number of arguments.

params.name: callback_name
params.desc: The name of the callback method to be invoked from the html dialog.

returns.desc: true if action added successfully, false otherwise.

methods.example:
Ruby Code
dialog.add_action_callback("say") { |action_context, param1, param2|
  puts "JavaScript said #{param1} and #{param2}"
}
dialog.show # should be called directly after binding callbacks
notes: When an HtmlDialog is closed, all callbacks to that instance are cleared. Attach or re-attach them before you show the dialog.

methods.name: bring_to_front

When use_content_size is set to false (the default value), the size dimensions will represent the outer frame size.

SketchUp 2022.0 fixed a bug where max_height and max_width were swapped when use_content_size was set to true.
SketchUp 2022.0 fixed a bug where use_content_size was not persisted (when preferences_key is set).
