methods.example:
dialog.set_on_closed do
  File.delete('temp_file.txt') if File.exist?('temp_file.txt')
end
notes: For saving state before window closes use #set_can_close instead.

methods.name: set_position
methods.summary: The #set_position method is used to set the position of the HtmlDialog relative to the screen, in pixels.

params.name: left
params.desc: The number of pixels from the left.

params.name: top
params.desc: The number of pixels from the top of the screen.

returns.desc: This always return true, never false.

bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2021.1, on Windows, calling this method incorrectly set the focus on the UI::HtmlDialog.
methods.example: dialog.set_position(100, 50)

methods.name: set_size
methods.summary: The #set_size method is used to set the outer frame size of the HtmlDialog, in pixels.

params.name: width
params.desc: Outer frame width of the HtmlDialog.

params.name: height
params.desc: Outer frame height of the HtmlDialog.

returns.desc: This always return true, never false.

bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2021.1, on Windows, calling this method incorrectly set the focus on the UI::HtmlDialog.
methods.example: dialog.set_size(320, 240)

methods.name: set_url
methods.summary: The #set_url method is used to load a HtmlDialog with the content at a specific URL. This method allows you to load web sites in a HtmlDialog.

params.name: url
params.desc: The URL for a specific web site.

methods.example: dialog.set_url("https://www.sketchup.com")

methods.name: show
methods.summary: The #show method is used to display a non-modal dialog box.
methods.example: dialog.show

methods.name: show_modal
methods.summary: The #show_modal method is used to display a modal dialog box.
methods.example: dialog.show_modal

methods.name: visible?
methods.summary: The #visible? method is useful to tell if the dialog is shown and still alive, if the dialog is minimized or not visible on the screen this will still return true.

returns.desc: Returns true if the dialog is open.

methods.example:
if dialog.visible?
  dialog.bring_to_front
else
  dialog = UI::HtmlDialog.new
  dialog.set_url("https://www.sketchup.com")
  dialog.show
end

UI::Notification.summary: UI::Notification objects allows you to show native notifications in the desktop. Notifications can have a message, icon and accept and/or dismiss buttons with callback blocks. Supported icon formats include: .bmp, .png, .jpg. Vector icons are supported as .svg on Windows and .pdf on Mac. Recommended icon size is 48x48 pixels. Icons larger than these sizes will be automatically downscaled to fit within the limits.

methods.name: icon_name
methods.summary: Instance Methods Gets the icon name, this is the path that will be used to get the icon from the file system path.

methods.name: icon_name=
methods.summary: Sets the icon path, this icon will be loaded from the path give, the path has to be a local filesystem path.

params.name: icon_name
params.desc: String providing the icon filesystem path.

methods.name: icon_tooltip
methods.summary: Gets the icon Tooltip, this is the string that appear when the mouse is over the icon.

methods.name: icon_tooltip=
methods.summary: Sets the icon Tooltip, this string will appear when the mouse is over the icon.

params.name: icon_tooltip
params.desc: String providing the new icon Tooltip.

methods.name: initialize
signatures: initialize(sketchup_extension, message = nil, icon_name = nil, icon_tooltip = nil)
methods.summary: Creates a new UI::Notification object.

params.name: sketchup_extension
params.desc: SketchupExtension instance used to identify the source of the notification.

params.name: message
params.desc: Message to display.

params.name: icon_name
params.desc: Path to an icon to display along with the message.

params.name: icon_tooltip
params.desc: Tooltip for the icon.

bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2018 messages could only be 3 lines long on Windows and 2 lines on Mac. Now the notification expands to fit its content.

Prior to SketchUp 2021.1 SketchUp could crash if the UI::Notification object is garbaged collected while it has notifications displayed on the screen. This could happen if the UI::Notification object ...
notes: In order to insert line breaks into the message you need to use \\r\\n. From SketchUp 2019 and onwards \\n also works on both Mac and Windows.

methods.name: message
methods.summary: Gets the message as string.

methods.name: message=
methods.summary: Sets a new message. Notifications are meant for quick and brief messages. These message disappear automatically after a short while if they are not interacted with.

params.name: message
params.desc: String providing the new message.

notes: In order to insert line breaks into the message you need to use \\r\\n. From SketchUp 2019 and onwards \\n also works on both Mac and Windows.

methods.name: on_accept
methods.summary: Shows a button in the notification with the given title and callback block, both arguments are required.

params.name: title
params.desc: Sets the title of the button.

params.name: block
params.desc: Sets the action callback, this will be called when the user clicks on the accept button.

bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2019 both the Accept and Dismiss buttons were displayed, even if only one had been implemented.
raises: [RuntimeError] When calling on_accept when the notification has already been shown.

methods.name: on_accept_title
methods.summary: Returns the accept's button title.

methods.name: on_dismiss
methods.summary: Shows a button in the notification with the given title and callback block. Both arguments are required. This callback is only called if you press the Dismiss button, not when the time runs out and the notification automatically disappears.

params.name: title
params.desc: Sets the title of the button.

params.name: block
params.desc: Sets the action callback, this will be called when the user clicks on the dismiss button.

bugs: Prior to SketchUp 2019 both the accept and dismiss buttons were displayed, even if only one had been implemented.
raises: [RuntimeError] When calling on_dismiss when the notification has already been shown.

methods.name: on_dismiss_title
methods.summary: Returns the dismiss's button title.

methods.name: show
methods.summary: Shows the notification. If not interacted with, the notification will disappear without calling any callbacks.
bugs: If assigned to a local variable SketchUp might crash prior to SketchUp 2021.1. See #initialize for more details.

UI::Toolbar.summary: The Toolbar class contains methods to create and manipulate SketchUp toolbars in Ruby. Toolbars are collections of buttons that you can use to activate custom Tools or ruby scripts. Also see the Command object for details on creating "commands" which can be called from your toolbars.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Class Methods The new method creates a new Toolbar object.

params.name: toolbarname
params.desc: The name for the new toolbar.

returns.desc: the newly created toolbar object

methods.example: toolbar = UI::Toolbar.new "Test"

methods.name: add_item
methods.summary: Instance Methods The add_item method is used to add an item to the toolbar.

params.name: command
params.desc: A Command object representing the command to add to the toolbar.

returns.desc: the toolbar where the command was just added

methods.example: toolbar = toolbar.add_item command

methods.name: add_separator
methods.summary: The add_separator method is used to add a line separator to the toolbar.

returns.desc: the toolbar where the line separator was just added

methods.example: toolbar = toolbar.add_separator

methods.name: count
methods.summary: The #count method is inherited from the Enumerable mix-in module.
methods.example: number = toolbar.count

methods.name: each
methods.summary: The #each method is used to iterate through all of the commands attached to a toolbar.
methods.example:
toolbar = UI::Toolbar.new "Test"
# This command displays Hello World on the screen when clicked
cmd = UI::Command.new("Test") { UI.messagebox("Hello World") }
toolbar.add_item cmd
toolbar = toolbar.add_separator
cmd = UI::Command.new("Test 2") { UI.messagebox("Hello World 2") }
toolbar.add_item cmd
toolbar.show
toolbar.each { | item |
  puts item
}

methods.name: get_last_state
methods.summary: The get_last_state method is used to determine if the toolbar was hidden or visible in the previous session of SketchUp. Valid states are TB_VISIBLE (1) for visible, TB_HIDDEN (0) for hidden, TB_NEVER_SHOWN (-1) for before never shown.

returns.desc: the last state of the toolbar (see constants above)

methods.example:
state = toolbar.get_last_state
case state
when TB_VISIBLE
  puts "Toolbar was visible in the last session."
when TB_HIDDEN
  puts "Toolbar was hidden in the last session."
when TB_NEVER_SHOWN
  puts "Toolbar was never shown in the last session."
else
  puts "Unknown toolbar state: #{state}"
end

methods.name: hide
methods.summary: The hide method is used to hide the toolbar on the user interface.
methods.example:
toolbar = UI::Toolbar.new "Test"
# This toolbar icon simply displays Hello World on the screen
cmd = UI::Command.new("Test") {
  UI.messagebox "Hello World"
}
cmd.small_icon = "ToolPencilSmall.png"
cmd.large_icon = "ToolPencilLarge.png"
cmd.tooltip = "Test Toolbars"
cmd.status_bar_text = "Testing the toolbars class"
cmd.menu_text = "Test"
toolbar = toolbar.add_item cmd
toolbar.show
UI.messagebox "Toolbar Showing"
toolbar.hide
UI.messagebox "Toolbar Hidden"

methods.name: length
methods.summary: The #length method returns the number of items in the toolbar.
methods.example: number = toolbar.length

methods.name: name
methods.summary: The name method returns the name of the toolbar.

returns.desc: the name of the toolbar.

methods.example:
toolbar = UI::Toolbar.new "Test"
# This command displays Hello World on the screen when clicked
cmd = UI::Command.new("Test") { UI.messagebox("Hello World") }
toolbar.add_item cmd
toolbar = toolbar.add_separator
cmd = UI::Command.new("Test 2") { UI.messagebox("Hello World 2") }
puts toolbar.name
toolbar.show

methods.name: restore
methods.summary: The restore method is used to reposition the toolbar to its previous location and show if not hidden.
methods.example: toolbar.restore

methods.name: show
methods.summary: The show method is used to display the toolbar in the user interface.
methods.example:
toolbar = UI::Toolbar.new "Test"
# This toolbar icon simply displays Hello World on the screen
cmd = UI::Command.new("Test") {
  UI.messagebox "Hello World"
}
cmd.small_icon = "ToolPencilSmall.png"
cmd.large_icon = "ToolPencilLarge.png"
cmd.tooltip = "Test Toolbars"
cmd.status_bar_text = "Testing the toolbars class"
cmd.menu_text = "Test"
toolbar = toolbar.add_item cmd
toolbar.show

methods.name: size
methods.summary: The #size method is an alias of #length.
methods.example: number = toolbar.size

methods.name: visible?
methods.summary: The visible? method is used to find out if a toolbar is currently visible.
methods.example: visible = toolbar.visible?

UI::WebDialog.summary: The Ruby WebDialog class allows you to create and interact with DHTML dialog boxes from Ruby. If your goal is to simply display a website to your users, consider using UI.openURL, which will show them a web page in their default browser rather than inside a dialog in SketchUp.

methods.name: add_action_callback
methods.summary: Instance Methods The add_action_callback method establishes a Ruby callback method that your web dialog can call to perform some function. Use the skp:callback_method_name to invoke the callback method from your webdialog. Your JavaScript in the webdialog will invoke the callback method with a string representing arguments to the callback method.

params.name: callback_name
params.desc: The name of the callback method to be invoked from the webdialog.

returns.desc: nil

methods.name: allow_actions_from_host
methods.summary: By default, actions are only allowed on the host where the webdialog is displayed. The allow_actions_from_host method is used to selectively allow actions to take place on a host remote from the host where the webdialog exists. If the webdialog is local, no remote host is allowed unless you use this method.

params.name: hostname
params.desc: The name (domain) of the host that your webdialog can access safely.

methods.example: dialog.allow_actions_from_host("sketchup.com")

methods.name: bring_to_front
methods.summary: The bring_to_front method is used to bring the webdialog to the front of all the windows on the desktop. See show_modal for how to ensure that your WedDialogs are on top.
methods.example: dialog.bring_to_front

methods.name: close
methods.summary: The close method is used to close the webdialog.
methods.example: dialog.close

methods.name: execute_script
methods.summary: The execute_script method is used to execute a JavaScript string on the web dialog.

params.name: script
params.desc: The JavaScript script to execute on the webdialog.

methods.example: js_command = "document.getElementById('id').innerHTML = 'Hi!'" dialog.execute_script(js_command)

methods.name: get_default_dialog_color
methods.summary: The get_default_dialog_color method is used to get the default dialog color for the web dialog.

returns.desc: a six digit hexidecimal number representing the color

methods.example:
dialog.get_default_dialog_color
#ece9d8

methods.name: get_element_value
methods.summary: The get_element_value method is used to get a value, with a given element_id, from the web dialog's DOM.

params.name: element_id
params.desc: The name of the element in your HTML code.

returns.desc: a string containing the retrieved value.

methods.example:
# In Ruby code:
dialog.get_element_value("myTextInput")

# In webdialog's HTML:
<input type="text" id="myTextInput" value="hello">

methods.name: initialize
signatures: initialize(dialog_title = "", scrollable = true, pref_key = nil, width = 250, height = 250, left = 0, top = 0, resizable = true)
methods.summary: The new method is used to create a new webdialog.

params.name: dialog_title
params.desc: The title to be displayed in the webdialog.

params.name: scrollable
params.desc: true if you want to allow scrollbars, false if you do not want to allow scrollbars.

params.name: pref_key
params.desc: The registry entry where the location and size of the dialog will be saved. If preferences_key is not included, the location and size will not be stored.

params.name: width
params.desc: The width of the webdialog.

params.name: height
params.desc: The height of the webdialog.

params.name: left
params.desc: The number of pixels from the left.

params.name: top
params.desc: The number of pixels from the top.

params.name: resizable
params.desc: true if you want the webdialog to be resizable, false if not.

params.name: properties
params.desc: A hash containing the initial properties of the newly created dialog.

methods.example:
dlg = UI::WebDialog.new("Show sketchup.com", true,
  "ShowSketchupDotCom", 739, 641, 150, 150, true);
dlg.set_url "https://www.sketchup.com"
dlg.show
notes: Since SU2017 the position and size of the dialog is DPI aware - it will scale to the DPI of the monitor automatically. Specify units as they would be on a traditional low-DPI monitor.
The browser which is embedded inside the dialog depends on the user's OS. On Mac, Safari is embedded, while on the PC whatever version of Internet Explorer is installed will be embedded.

options.desc: (true)
(false)
(false)

methods.name: max_height
methods.summary: The max_height method is used to get the maximum height that the user is allowed to resize the dialog to.

returns.desc: the maximum height in pixels

methods.example: max = dialog.max_height

methods.name: max_height=
methods.summary: The max_height= method is used to set the maximum height that the user is allowed to resize the dialog to.

params.name: height
params.desc: The maximum height in pixels

methods.example: dialog.max_height = 400
notes: As of SU2017 this will automatically scale the height by the same factor as UI.scale_factor.

methods.name: max_width
methods.summary: The max_width method is used to get the maximum width that the user is allowed to resize the dialog to.

returns.desc: the maximum width in pixels

methods.example: max = dialog.max_width

methods.name: max_width=
methods.summary: The max_width= method is used to set the maximum width that the user is allowed to resize the dialog to.

params.name: width
params.desc: The maximum width in pixels

methods.example: dialog.max_width = 500
notes: As of SU2017 this will automatically scale the width by the same factor as UI.scale_factor.

methods.name: min_height
methods.summary: The min_width method is used to get the minimum height that the user is allowed to resize the dialog to.

returns.desc: the minimum height in pixels

methods.example: min = dialog.min_height

methods.name: min_height=
methods.summary: The min_height= method is used to set the minimum height that the user is allowed to resize the dialog to.

params.name: height
params.desc: The minimum height in pixels

methods.example: dialog.min_height = 100
notes: As of SU2017 this will automatically scale the height by the same factor as UI.scale_factor.

methods.name: min_width
methods.summary: The min_width method is used to get the minimum width that the user is allowed to resize the dialog to.

returns.desc: the minimum width in pixels

methods.example: min = dialog.min_width

methods.name: min_width=
methods.summary: The min_width= method is used to set the minimum width that the user is allowed to resize the dialog to.

params.name: width
params.desc: The minimum width in pixels

methods.example: dialog.min_width = 200
notes: As of SU2017 this will automatically scale the width by the same factor as UI.scale_factor.

methods.name: navigation_buttons_enabled=
methods.summary: The navigation_buttons_enabled= method is used to set whether the home, next, and back buttons are visible at the top of the WebDialog on the mac. This method has no use on the PC, as these buttons are never displayed.
methods.example: dialog.navigation_buttons_enabled = false

methods.name: navigation_buttons_enabled?
methods.summary: The navigation_buttons_enabled? method is used to get whether the home, next, and back buttons are visible at the top of the WebDialog on the mac. This method has no use on the PC, as these buttons are never displayed. On the mac, this defaults to true for new WebDialogs.
methods.example: nav_buttons = dialog.navigation_buttons_enabled?

methods.name: post_url
methods.summary: The post_url method is used to send the data to a url using the HTTP POST method.

params.name: url
params.desc: The url to send the data.

params.name: data
params.desc: The data to be sent.

methods.example: data = dialog.post_url("https://www.mydomain.com/formchecker.cgi",data)

methods.name: screen_scale_factor
methods.summary: The screen_scale_factor method returns the ratio of screen pixels to logical window units (called 'points' on Mac) for the screen this WebDialog is currently in. On a retina screen Mac, this ratio will be greater than 1.0. On Windows this always return 1.0.

returns.desc: screen scale factor

methods.example: factor = dialog.screen_scale_factor

methods.name: set_background_color
methods.summary: The set_background_color method is used to set the background color for the webdialog.

params.name: color
params.desc: A six digit hexidecimal color.

methods.example: dlg.set_background_color("f3f0f0")

methods.name: set_file
methods.summary: The #set_file method is used to identify a local HTML file to display in the webdialog.

params.name: filename
params.desc: The filename for the webdialog file (HTML file).

params.name: path
params.desc: A path that filename is relative to.

methods.example:
file = File.join(__dir__, 'mypage.html')
dialog.set_file(file)

methods.name: set_full_security
methods.summary: The set_full_security method is used to place the WebDialog into a higher security mode where remote URLs and plugins (such as Flash) are not allowed inside the browser. This defaults to false when a new WebDialog is created.

returns.desc: the updated WebDialog

methods.example: dialog.set_full_security

methods.name: set_html
methods.summary: The set_html method is used to load a webdialog with a string of provided HTML.

params.name: html_string
params.desc: A string of valid html to display in your webdialog.

methods.example: html= 'Hello world!' dialog.set_html(html)

methods.name: set_on_close
methods.summary: The set_on_close method is used to establish one or more activities to perform when the dialog closes (such as saving values stored in the dialog).
methods.example: dialog.set_on_close{ UI.messagebox("Closing the webDialog") }
notes: UI::WebDialog#close method should not be called from the UI::WebDialog#set_on_close callback. That would make it trigger itself recursively.

methods.name: set_position
methods.summary: The set_position method is used to set the position of the webdialog relative to the screen, in pixels.

params.name: left
params.desc: The number of pixels from the left.

params.name: top
params.desc: The number of pixels from the top of the screen.

methods.example: dialog.set_position(100,50)
notes: As of SU2017 this will automatically scale the x and y by the same factor as UI.scale_factor.

methods.name: set_size
methods.summary: The set_size method is used to set the size of the webdialog, in pixels.

params.name: w
params.desc: Width of the webdialog.

params.name: h
params.desc: Height of the webdialog.

methods.example: dialog.set_size(320,240)
notes: As of SU2017 this will automatically scale the width and height by the same factor as UI.scale_factor.

methods.name: set_url
methods.summary: The set_url method is used to load a webdialog with the content at a specific URL. This method allows you to load web sites in a webdialog.

params.name: url
params.desc: The URL for a specific web site.

methods.example: dialog.set_url "https://www.sketchup.com"

methods.name: show
methods.summary: The show method is used to display a non-modal dialog box.

methods.name: show_modal
methods.summary: The show_modal method is used to display a modal dialog box. In SketchUp 6 and 7, this behaves differently on Mac vs. PC. On the PC, it shows a truly modal dialog, meaning so long as the WebDialog is visible, no input can be performed elsewhere inside SketchUp. On the Mac, "modal" WebDialogs do not behave this way, but instead are "always on top" of other windows.

methods.name: visible?
methods.summary: The visible? method is used to tell if the webdialog is currently shown.
methods.example: vis = dialog.visible?

methods.name: write_image
signatures: write_image(image_path, option, top_left_x, top_left_y, bottom_right_x, bottom_right_y)
methods.summary: The write_image method is used to grab a portion of the web dialog screen and save the image to the given file path.

params.name: image_path
params.desc: The destination path of the saved image.

params.name: option
params.desc: Specifies what method to use when saving the image. For JPG/JPEG images, this specifies the image quality and can range from 1 to 100. For PNG images this specifies the compression algorithm: <4 ...

params.name: top_left_x
params.desc: The x coordinate of the upper left corner of the region to grab.

params.name: top_left_y
params.desc: The x coordinate of the upper left corner of the region to grab.

params.name: bottom_right_x
params.desc: The x coordinate of the lower right corner of the region to grab.

params.name: bottom_right_y
params.desc: The x coordinate of the lower right corner of the region to grab.

methods.example:
dialog.write_image('c:/grab.jpg', 70, 0, 0, 100, 100)
dialog.write_image('c:/grab.png', 4, 0, 0, 100, 100)
